## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix complete singly pointed Heegaard data of any closed oriented three-manifold, a surface complex structure $j$, protected nearly symmetric geometry and exact product generator charts. Let $J_n(s,t)$ converge smoothly with all derivatives to $J_\infty(s,t)$, with uniformly bounded coefficients in one small fixed Cayley neighborhood of that background. Suppose there are autonomous paths $J_n^\pm(t)\to J_\infty^\pm(t)$ such that $J_n(s,t)-J_n^\pm(t)$ tends to zero, with every coefficient derivative, as $s\to\pm\infty$, UNIFORMLY in $n$. This includes families which are exactly autonomous outside one common compact transition interval, and also rapidly decaying source perturbations and their compact-transition truncations. On all protected sets, including every exact generator chart, these structures agree with the common background. At $t=0,1$ their full boundary structures agree with the common background, independently of $s,n$. All source derivatives are uniformly bounded. Let $u_n$ be actual smooth finite-energy solutions of $u_s+J_n(s,t,u)u_t=0$, with the physical product-torus boundaries, generator ends, $n_z(u_n)=0$ and $E(u_n)\le E_0<\infty$.

A subsequence converges to one ANCHORED central strip $u_0$ solving the $J_\infty(s,t)$ equation, possibly constant, together with finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^-_\infty$ strip levels preceding it and finitely many ordered nonconstant $J^+_\infty$ strip levels following it. No nonconstant sphere or boundary-disk bubbles occur. All adjoining generator ends match, the complete energy is the sum of those of these components, and all intervening necks and outer tails lose neither energy nor image diameter. The central map is not divided by translation. Each nonconstant end level is specified up to its ordinary translation. Central convergence and translated end-level convergence are smooth on compact sets, including the physical boundaries.

Eventually the continuous Whitney class of $u_n$ is the concatenation of the ordered end levels, the central class and the remaining end levels. Their actual fixed-end Fredholm indices add to $\operatorname{ind}P_{u_n}$. Here the source-dependent central operator is an actual Fredholm $H^1\to L^2$ operator, with the same kernel/cokernel in its integer higher realizations; its index is the same geometric Whitney index used for the autonomous levels. No regularity, sign of a central index, finite moduli count, gluing collar or chain-map assertion is assumed or concluded.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The uniform asymptotically autonomous tails, coefficient convergence, complete cut systems with the one zero mark in each cut component, uniform energy bound, physical boundaries and generator ends. The nearly symmetric structures have one fixed integrable surface background; interpolation inside their stated small Cayley neighborhood preserves the protected values and generator charts.

[F1] General smooth complex strip bundles with totally real boundary planes and exact transverse product ends admit actual global frames and Fredholm operators. The result concerns bundle-symbol operators, not only autonomous holomorphic zeros. Integer higher domains impose only the original zeroth boundary trace. ([[lem-geometric-strip-linearization-frame-and-fredholm-index]], [[lem-strip-fredholm-index-agrees-in-higher-sobolev-spaces]])

[F2] The actual source-dependent interior and physical-boundary epsilon estimates hold under uniform coefficient bounds and fixed boundary structures. ([[lem-interior-energy-regularity-for-smooth-almost-complex-strips]], [[lem-boundary-energy-regularity-for-totally-real-strips]]) Local bounded-energy compactness, rescaling and the interior and boundary soft-rescaling proofs allow smoothly source-dependent almost complex structures. Their local energy-atom inductions give finite sphere/disk trees and full energy and node identities near every actual concentration point. Small-energy necks lose neither energy nor image diameter. ([[lem-smooth-strip-compactness-away-from-energy-concentration]], [[lem-soft-rescaling-captures-isolated-interior-energy-atoms]], [[lem-soft-rescaling-captures-isolated-totally-real-boundary-energy-atoms]], [[lem-small-local-energy-cylinder-neck-collapse]])

[F3] The actual autonomous strip compactness proof uses finite disjoint bad windows, bounded-offset clusters and collapsing generator necks; its quantitative small-window estimate is also available. ([[thm-countable-choice-bubbled-transverse-strip-breaking-compactness]], [[lem-small-local-energy-transverse-strip-neck-collapse]])

[F4] Point-divisor degree is the curvature integral of an actually constructed line-bundle connection flat near the physical tori and generator charts. The integrand is bounded by a constant times the Dirichlet energy density. Compact bubble domains are nonnegative; a sphere or one-torus disk with zero degree at a mark meeting each cut component is constant. ([[lem-divisor-degree-additivity-and-zero-marked-strip-bubble-exclusion]])

[F5] Finite-energy autonomous strip ends converge to generators and in exact product charts have all-order exponential expansions. Continuous classes have actual smooth relative models, homotopy-invariant additive geometric index, and the cutoff concatenation proof identifies actual unbubbled limits with their continuous class concatenations. ([[lem-finite-energy-transverse-strip-end-convergence]], [[lem-product-integrable-transverse-strip-end-exponential-asymptotics]], [[lem-continuous-whitney-classes-admit-relative-smooth-fixed-end-models]], [[lem-smooth-relative-whitney-homotopies-preserve-strip-fredholm-index]], [[lem-unbubbled-strip-breaking-and-regular-gluing-preserve-whitney-concatenation]])

## Proof

1.1 In genus zero the target is a point: every map is constant, its section spaces are zero, and the entire assertion follows with no end levels and index zero. Assume positive genus for the remaining proof. The actual central linearization has formula $P_u\xi=\nabla_s\xi+J(s,t,u)\nabla_t\xi+(\nabla_\xi J)(s,t,u)u_t$; differentiating the map variable introduces no derivative of the prescribed source arguments. Its real principal symbol is exactly the Cauchy--Riemann symbol. Uniform generator ends put each far tail inside its exact product chart, where the equation and its coordinate linearization are exactly $D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t$, with real and imaginary boundary planes. The transverse end expansion in [F5] applies there. The bundle-symbol assertion of [F1] therefore gives the actual Fredholm operator and higher range agreement. To identify its index, first flatten the exponential tails to their generators by scalar cutoffs inside those product charts. The index is unchanged: the completed squared boundary phase loop is homotoped only inside the same fixed end chart, where the two added cap phases cancel. Interpolate the prescribed $J(s,t)$ to the fixed background using its small Cayley coefficients; all generator charts and boundary end values stay fixed. A joint complex frame on the compact nonconstant core is constructed by the finite projection ODE in [F1]. The completed boundary phase consequently varies by a genuine loop homotopy. Its winding, hence actual index, is constant. The flattened map now has exactly the smooth relative index in [F5], so the central index is the geometric Whitney index, including for nonautonomous solutions. This proves the claimed operator assertion without importing an autonomous-solution hypothesis. [F1, F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Apply [F2]'s local energy estimates and Sobolev bootstrap on each compact rectangle. Countable diagonal extraction gives smooth convergence off finitely many energy concentrations on each such rectangle, and finite total energy bounds their total number by $E_0/h$, with the positive local bubble quantum $h$. At an interior concentration use the actual interior soft-rescaling induction; at a physical edge use its boundary version. Those are local disk/half-disk arguments. They do not impose an artificial totally real condition on the curved boundary of a chosen local half-disk or on a rectangle's vertical cuts. This gives the actual finite bubble trees, their full energy identities and connecting collapsed necks at every finite concentration. The remaining anchored map solves the limiting source-dependent equation smoothly after the actual puncture-removal step in those proofs. Its energy is finite. The small-window estimate needed here and below does not require an autonomous source. Indeed [F2]'s actual source-dependent epsilon estimates bound $|du|$ by $C\sqrt\delta$ on every buffered window of energy $\delta$. Every angular slice then has small length. Compactness of the two boundaries and their finite transverse intersection force its two endpoints into one of the finitely many separated generator neighborhoods; the entire short slice remains in that chart. Connectedness forces a whole connected small-window neck into one chart. There the equation is EXACTLY $D_0v=0$, since all prescribed source-dependent structures agree with $i$ on that chart. The actual Fourier proof in [F3] then gives the same energy and diameter decay, with uniform constants. For the finite-energy central map all sufficiently far windows have arbitrarily small energy, so each whole tail lies in one chart. Slice Poincare and the positive spectral gap give its generator limit and all-order exponential expansion by [F5]. This proves the central end assertion without an autonomous-source end theorem being applied outside its hypotheses. It may be constant, and that possibility is retained as the anchored central component. No translation of this compact source core has been made. [F2, F3, F5, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Account for every component escaping to longitudinal infinity. Fix the bad-window threshold $\delta>0$ from [F3] and retain the source interval $[-10,10]$ as an anchor. The continuous function $A_n(s)=E(u_n;[s-2,s+2]\times[0,1])$ tends to zero on both infinite tails, so $B_n=\{s:A_n(s)\ge\delta\}$ is compact. If it is nonempty, select its least point, then the least remaining point at least four to its right, and continue. The corresponding windows have disjoint interiors, so there are at most $\lfloor E_0/\delta\rfloor$ selections. Every point of $B_n$ lies between a selected point and four units to its right, since otherwise it would be an available next selection. Include the anchor at zero in the finite cluster list, whether or not it is bad. After subsequences their bounded-offset clusters either remain at a bounded distance from the anchor or escape to one of the two infinities. Bounded clusters are already part of step 1.2. Each escaping cluster, translated to its center, has on every fixed source rectangle coefficients converging with every derivative to $J^-_\infty$ or $J^+_\infty$, by the uniform tail hypothesis. Thus [F3]'s same local extraction, rescaling and end argument gives a finite-energy strip level there with its possible local bubble trees; before bubble exclusion that strip may be constant if a bubble carries the cluster energy. Different clusters have distances tending to infinity. Between clusters, beyond the outermost clusters and between the anchor and its nearest clusters every fixed-size window is below the common threshold. The actual source-dependent small-window argument proved in step 1.2 puts every buffered long gap inside one exact generator chart and makes its central energy and diameter tend to zero. The finite energy identity inside the retained cores then captures ALL energy; there is no residual escaping component or neck energy. The matching generator limits agree because each connecting image diameter tends to zero. The escaping limit levels themselves are autonomous by coefficient convergence. The finite-window extraction and source-dependent neck argument do not require exact autonomy of each approximating map, and keep the central core anchored. [F2, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Now eliminate all the bubble trees, rather than assuming their absence in the extraction. Use [F4]'s connection for the fixed divisor $E_z$. It is independent of the source and is flat near the tori and generator charts. Integrals over the smooth component cores converge. The absolute integral over any omitted neck or energy tail is bounded by its energy times one common curvature bound, and tends to zero by steps 1.2 and 2.1. The frame-Stokes formula in [F4] therefore expresses the integer $n_z(u_n)=0$ as the sum of the degrees of the central strip, every end level and every actual compact sphere or disk bubble. This argument uses a fixed TARGET line bundle and no autonomous-source or squared-determinant index connection. Every term is nonnegative by protected-divisor positivity for strips and by the compact bubble positivity in [F4]. Hence each compact bubble has zero mark degree. For a sphere its domain is $d\Sigma$; for a one-torus disk its domain is constant on each cut component. The chosen $z$ meets the sole cut component of either complete system. [F4] then makes every such zero-mark bubble constant. The local stability rules remove all remaining ghost-only trees: a finite tree of constant bubbles with no active component has a terminal component with too few distinguished points, contrary to the explicitly stabilized extraction. Thus there are no bubble trees. Each escaping cluster retains at least $\delta$ energy on a sufficiently large fixed translated core by its bad center and local energy identity; with bubbles excluded its strip level is therefore nonconstant. Only the anchored central component may remain constant. Steps 1.2 and 2.1 now give exactly the smooth central and end components, energy identity and matched necks in the Statement. [F4, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix sufficiently far generator cuts on each of the finitely many limiting components. They and all the connecting necks lie in the same exact product charts for large $n$, by step 3.1. Multiply the coordinate maps on successive necks by real scalar cutoffs, retaining their two physical boundary planes and contracting their middle portions to the common generator. This is an actual continuous relative homotopy, with the outer ends fixed. On every retained finite core the sequence is uniformly close to its limit. The boundary-preserving local-addition straight homotopy identifies these cores with the limiting ones; the remaining finite cutoff tails are homotoped inside their product charts. This is precisely the topological construction in [F5]'s actual class-splitting proof, which uses only core convergence, physical boundary preservation and collapsed generator necks, not autonomy of the central equation. Consequently $[u_n]$ is eventually the ordered concatenation of the end classes with the anchored central class. Apply the additive continuous Whitney index from [F5] and the actual source-dependent operator identification in step 1.1. This gives the asserted equality of actual indices. A constant central component has the constant transverse $D_0$ operator and index zero, so retaining it contributes no false translation parameter or index shift. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual complete pointed closed Heegaard diagram, a positive surface area form $\eta$, and one point $q_R$ in each complementary region, including its basepoint $z$. Let $j_a$ be a smooth compact finite-parameter family of positive surface structures and let $X_a=\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma,j_a)$. Supply actual smooth relative transports $\Phi_a:X_*\to X_a$ with smooth equivariant ordered lifts, preserving the discriminant and every $E_{q_R}$, raw-identity near both tori and common exact generator charts. Such families may be constructed by the finite-parameter transport lemma along prescribed paths from a fixed reference parameter. No arbitrary boundary trivialization is presumed.

Let $a(s)$ be a smooth profile constant at both source ends. On $X_*$ consider an actual smooth finite-energy fixed-end solution
$$u_s+K_{s,t}(u)u_t=W_s(u),\qquad u(s,0)\in L_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in L_\beta.$$
Here $W$ is smooth, independent of $t$, compactly supported in $s$, zero near both tori and the common generator charts, and has a smooth permutation-equivariant ordered lift preserving all pairwise diagonals and coordinate incidence sets. The physical vertical structures $(\Phi_{a(s)})_*K_{s,t}$ equal $\operatorname{Sym}^g(j_{a(s)})$ near the protected discriminant and incidence divisors, tame the descended fixed product area form elsewhere, and have the stated common fixed full boundary structure and generator charts. Take uniform smooth bounds and taming constants on the actual compact parameter families under consideration. Uniform generator limits at both ends are required.

Every region multiplicity is nonnegative. There is a finite smooth branched ordered cover of the strip, and
$$E(u)\le C\left(\sum_R n_R(u)\operatorname{Area}_\eta(R)+\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(|a'(s)|^2+\|\widetilde W_s\|_\infty^2\bigr)\,ds\right),$$
where $\widetilde W$ is the supplied ordered lift and $C$ is uniform on the stated compact families. If the fixed diagram is globally weakly admissible and $n_z=0$, only finitely many such integral domains occur across all endpoint pairs, without an index restriction; consequently these actual solutions have a uniform energy bound whenever the displayed forcing integral is uniformly bounded. Genus zero is the one-point case. No map counts, relative grading or invariance conclusion is included.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] Actual finite-parameter relative coefficient atlases, smooth transports and equivariant ordered lifts exist, with the indicated divisor, diagonal, boundary and fixed-chart prescriptions. The actual two-torus extension provides common full boundary values and generator charts for compatible chosen families. ([[lem-finite-parameter-relative-symmetric-products-have-adapted-parallel-transports]], [[lem-relative-symmetric-product-families-admit-a-common-two-torus-boundary-structure]])

[F2] The scalar Cauchy–Riemann similarity theorem accepts bounded measurable zero-order coefficients and gives a continuous nonvanishing complex factor times a holomorphic function. Its Cauchy transform has actual local $W^{1,p}$ bounds. The weak CR, Morrey and smooth-bootstrap suppliers apply to continuous weak solutions. ([[lem-countable-choice-cauchy-riemann-similarity-and-unique-continuation]], [[lem-countable-choice-lp-regularity-for-small-strip-cauchy-riemann-coefficients]], [[lem-countable-choice-planar-morrey-estimate]], [[lem-continuous-weak-almost-complex-strip-solutions-are-smooth]])

[F3] Smooth degree equals signed regular-value count and the two-form integral; smooth Sard supplies common regular values under Countable Choice, and finite compact Stokes holds. Point-incidence lines have canonical boundary sections, integer relative degree and point-movement invariance. ([[lem-degree-is-well-defined-and-independent-of-the-normalized-top-form]], [[thm-regular-value-formula-for-compact-support-degree]], [[thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds]], [[lem-finite-chart-localization-defines-choice-free-integration-and-compact-stokes]], [[lem-symmetric-product-divisor-intersections-and-point-movement]])

[F4] On a globally weak complete closed diagram the actual normalized periodic lattice has no nonzero nonnegative real vector, and the nonnegative normalized affine domain sets across the finite endpoint pairs are finite. This finite lattice proof precedes all counts and uses the fixed surface and attaching circles. ([[thm-globally-weak-closed-heegaard-data-admit-a-finite-chosen-hat-complex]], full Proof2.1; [[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]])

[A1] Countable Choice is assumed; all additional covers, root monodromies and parameter normalizations are finite. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

**Given:** The actual data and Countable Choice in the Statement.

1.1 Pass to physical tuples $v=\Phi_{a(s)}u$. Their equation is $v_s+J_{s,t}v_t=B_s(v)$, where $B$ is the sum of the actual horizontal velocity of $\Phi_{a(s)}$ and $(\Phi_{a(s)})_*W_s$. By [F1] it has a smooth bounded equivariant ordered lift, with norm bounded by $C(|a'|+\|\widetilde W_s\|_\infty)$ and all prescribed coordinate incidences and diagonals invariant. In any relative support chart use its moving holomorphic coordinates $z_a$. The resulting coefficient equation is $c_s+i c_t=F(s,t,c)$ near the protected loci; the derivative of the coordinate with respect to $a$ is included in $F$, not discarded. Its ordered lift is again smooth and equivariant, with the same bound, since coordinate changes and their inverses have uniform derivatives on smaller compact charts. Every coordinate centered at $q_R$ keeps that point zero, so its corresponding lifted velocity vanishes when that coordinate is zero. [F1, A1, given, construct]

2.1 Prove the needed divisibility as a BOUNDED assertion, including higher collisions and arbitrary connection comparisons. Write the ordered velocity components as $V_i$. Swapping two roots gives $V_i(\mathbf z)=V_j(\operatorname{swap}_{ij}\mathbf z)$ by equivariance. The finite-dimensional mean-value inequality therefore gives $|V_i-V_j|\le C|z_i-z_j|$ on each smaller cluster chart. For the cluster discriminant $d=\prod_{i<j}(z_i-z_j)^2$, differentiation off its zero set gives $$\frac{V(d)}d=2\sum_{i<j}\frac{V_i-V_j}{z_i-z_j},$$ a uniformly bounded permutation-invariant function. It descends off the divisor and is defined to be zero on it, yielding a specified bounded measurable coefficient. The identity $V(d)=A d$ holds also at zeros: on the smooth discriminant part the field is tangent, and on its singular part the defining polynomial has zero differential. For an incidence equation $e=\prod_i z_i$, invariance first gives $V_i=0$ on $z_i=0$ where no other root is zero, then everywhere on that hyperplane by continuity. Hence $|V_i|\le C|z_i|$ and $V(e)/e=\sum_iV_i/z_i$ is bounded, with the same zero-set identity. Units from other support clusters add bounded logarithmic terms. Thus along the actual solution each local divisor equation satisfies $d_s+i d_t=A(s,t)d$, with locally bounded measurable coefficient, even when that coefficient has no smooth extension at collisions. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F2] in its scalar complex case. The local divisor equation is a continuous nonvanishing complex factor times a holomorphic scalar function. Its nonzero zeros are isolated and have positive integer local degree: the nonvanishing factor extends over the small disk and hence has zero boundary winding. Local containment propagates through each divisor neighborhood by this same factorization; a first exit from global containment is impossible, because the value at that point is still on the closed divisor and its protected neighborhood is open. Since both boundary tori and the uniform end generators miss every selected divisor and the discriminant, containment is excluded. Their preimages are consequently discrete. They lie in a bounded source interval by the uniform generator ends, and away from the physical boundary by compactness there and disjointness of the tori from the protected loci. Hence each preimage is finite. This proves nonnegative region multiplicities and the finite collision set without a transversality assumption. [F1, F2, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Off that finite collision set take the cover of all ordered roots, of degree $d=g!$; disconnected components are allowed. A puncture has finite permutation monodromy, and each cycle is filled with a source coordinate $\pi(\zeta)=\zeta^k$. The cover is orientation preserving and holomorphic in its source coordinates. Root continuity supplies continuous bounded extensions: on a sufficiently small support disk all roots in that cluster converge to its single limiting support point. On the punctured cover, in the moving holomorphic target coordinates each root has bounded $\partial_{\bar\zeta}$ derivative prescribed by the actual smooth ordered forcing and the derivative of $\pi$. This distribution identity extends over the filled point: integrate against a test on a punctured disk, and the omitted boundary integral tends to zero by the root bound times its circle length. Subtract the [F2] Cauchy transform of that bounded right side. The remaining bounded distributionally holomorphic function is smooth and removable at the center. Thus the roots belong to every local $W^{1,p}$, $p>2$. Their coupled forced equation has smooth coefficients in all root variables; either repeated differentiation with the same Cauchy bounds, or [F2]'s continuous-weak smooth bootstrap on its graph almost complex structure, gives smoothness of the complete ordered lift. This argument does not assert smooth root extraction for arbitrary smooth polynomial coefficient maps. [F1, F2, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 On this cover the lifted vertical structure is smooth and uniformly tame for $\Omega=\sum_i\eta_i$. Near collisions it is the product $j_{a(s)}$; off the protected diagonal neighborhood the quotient is a local finite covering on a compact set, so its inverse differential there has uniform bounds. The lifted equation is $f_s+\widetilde Jf_t=\widetilde B$. Tameness, bounded coefficients and Cauchy–Schwarz give $$c|f_t|^2\le\Omega(f_t,\widetilde Jf_t)=\Omega(f_s,f_t)-\Omega(\widetilde B,f_t),\qquad |df|^2\le C\bigl(\Omega(f_s,f_t)+|\widetilde B|^2\bigr).$$ The first identity fixes the sign convention $\Omega(w,Jw)>0$; absorb its last term by $xy\le\epsilon x^2+C_\epsilon y^2$, and use $f_s=-\widetilde Jf_t+\widetilde B$ for the second bound. Holomorphic source covering and conformal naturality multiply the integral forcing bound by $d$. The roots have finite energy on compact filled cores by step4.1 and on the tails by the local unramified generator charts and the assumed finite energy of $u$. The quotient differential itself is uniformly bounded in the actual compact relative charts, so $E(u)$ is bounded above by $C E(f)$ plus the same forcing integral. No inverse quotient bound at a collision is used. [F1, step 1.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 The physical boundary roots lie on the ORIGINAL attaching circles, since the transports and forcing are raw-identity or zero near both tori. For a region $R$, choose a common regular value of the finitely many smooth root maps away from branch values. Their local product-definer identity counts exactly $d$ lifts of each physical incidence intersection. To identify this with the prescribed region coefficient, move that regular test point to $q_R$ along a finite path inside $R$. The incidence line construction works jointly in the surface-family parameter and the moving point: center each local root coordinate at that point, and its overlap ratios are the smooth nonvanishing unit products described below. Pull back this actual line family by the physical section $v(s,t)$. Its canonical section is nonzero on the boundary throughout the point path, because the path misses both attaching systems. Thus its relative degree is constant by the finite frame-winding argument in [F3], even though the transports need not preserve incidence divisors of UNCHOSEN points. At $q_R$ the chosen divisor is preserved by the transport and this degree is $n_R(u)$. Consequently the signed root-degree sum over $R$ is exactly $d n_R(u)$. The preimages of curve edges contribute zero two-form integral: the pullback vanishes on the rank-deficient set, and at a rank-two point the inverse image of an edge is a local smooth arc, covered by countably many source charts. Hence [F3]'s two-form degree formula over the regions gives $$\int_F\sum_i f_i^*\eta=d\sum_R n_R(u)\operatorname{Area}_\eta(R).$$ This is a signed topological identity, not a holomorphic-area assertion. Degrees agree with those on the fixed reference target, with an actual line-family construction as follows. In centered root coordinates the local incidence definer is the constant polynomial coefficient. On an overlap a root change $h_a$ fixes zero, so $h_a(z)/z$ is a nonvanishing holomorphic unit; the product of these units over the cluster is symmetric and has a smooth coefficient expression by [F1]'s contour transition formula. Noncontaining clusters supply ordinary nonvanishing units. These are actual smooth line transition functions on the relative family, with its canonical section and the physical incidence coorientation. Pull this line family back by the actual transports. Finite local projections and their smooth ODE trivialize it along each parameter path, taking the canonical nonzero section as the fixed frame on a common neighborhood of both tori. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Supply an actual composable chosen decorated surface movie in S3 times an interval, with the good finite marked triangle and neck data, actual auxiliary top cycles, unit calibrations and diagram comparisons described in the proof. Suppose its knot endpoints have the normalized ordinary w and z gradings and original Seifert Alexander normalization. In particular a genus-g surface with disk w-region and connected genus-g z-region has a full-minus map of Maslov degree zero, nonnegative U exponents and Alexander upper shift g. An annulus with both regions disks has degree zero in both filtrations. This is a grading theorem for a supplied actual composite; existence of a compatible movie and its tower scalar are separate hypotheses and conclusions are not asserted for a merely formal tree word.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual composable chosen movie, its elementary count maps and comparisons, its genuine sector caps, its region decomposition and the endpoint normalization in the Statement.

[F1] [[lem-chosen-marked-link-triangles-define-chain-maps]] supplies its stated actual interface. No full decorated movie invariance is used.

[F2] [[lem-chosen-link-neck-maps-and-edge-counts-satisfy-local-identities]] supplies its stated actual interface. No full decorated movie invariance is used.

[F7] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] supplies its stated actual interface. No full decorated movie invariance is used.

## Proof

1.1 For each intermediate S3 multi-link diagram use its actual ordinary w complex and its actual ordinary z complex, obtained by setting the opposite color to one. Choose their absolute origins so their respective highest ordinary homology degrees are (n-1)/2, where n is the number of w marks, also the number of z marks. The highest classes and their identifications in the chosen data must be supplied by the actual ordinary operations, not assumed for an unconstructed diagram. For a band step, its actual squeeze comparison supplies those identifications. A different intermediate origin would change the two adjacent step shifts oppositely; no endpoint degree is being prescribed by this choice. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.2 Fix either color q=w or q=z separately. Its relative Maslov grading is the actual capped determinant index minus twice the q intersections. For two triangle terms in the chosen sector, glue their corner caps and connecting pair-strip caps. The matching boundary real frames cancel in pairs. The difference is the capped triply periodic chain, so the index difference is its Chern evaluation plus twice its q intersections. Thus, after subtracting the corner relative gradings and twice the marked exponent, the triangle operator has ONE constant c_q on that sector, independent of the chosen auxiliary input corner. This assertion uses determinant-line gluing, not counts or an arbitrary absolute triangle formula. Here the sector is genuine: each S3 end has unique Spin-c structure and the auxiliary unlink is nullhomologous in the split S1-times-S2 boundary, so BOTH the w and z auxiliary structures are explicitly the standard torsion structure. They are not inferred from one another by a false torsion implication for a homologically nontrivial link. The actual auxiliary filling uses three- and four-handles and yields S3-times-I. Its handle exact sequence shows H2(X) is generated by the attaching spheres from the auxiliary boundary: all H2 is killed by those three-handles and four-handles add none. Also X is the complement of a regular neighborhood of a one-complex in the product, so it is simply connected: a loop bounds a disk in the product, and a generic disk misses that one-complex since two plus one is less than four. Thus H2 has no invisible torsion pairing, and restriction H2-cohomology of X to the auxiliary boundary is injective. The standard torsion auxiliary restriction therefore fixes the same genuine extension sector for both input cycles. The cap-zero argument from the actual cut balls verifies its periodic Chern relations. Nothing requires c_w=c_z. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.3 Consequently for the actual index-zero triangle operator F, its q degree as a map with a homogeneous auxiliary input theta is Mq(theta)+c_q. This remains true after setting the opposite color to one: the surviving variable has degree minus two and exactly restores its removed marked exponent. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.4 The chosen auxiliary cycles Theta_w and Theta_z differ only in the alternating four-marked factor. Its actual index-one z bigon has n_w=0 and n_z=1, so its actual relative degrees give $M_w(\Theta_w)-M_w(\Theta_z)=1,\qquad M_z(\Theta_w)-M_z(\Theta_z)=-1.$ The same relative difference is retained by the actual marked neck transfers. No absolute half-degree for either auxiliary cycle is used. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.5 The NEW unit comparison proves that F(Theta_w,-) with all V equal to one is the actual ordinary w diagram comparison, with its top unit carried with coefficient one. This is a chain homotopy equivalence at the fixed ordinary w-pointed ends. Its degree is zero: a homogeneous isomorphism between the ordinary homology modules with highest degree normalized to the SAME (n-1)/2 must carry that highest degree to itself, and its unit coefficient is one. Hence M_w(Theta_w)+c_w=0. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.6 Apply literal w/z relabeling to the SAME NEW physical unit comparison. The strips, source junction, inverses, continuations and triangle collars are unchanged; their independent marked weights are relabeled. It proves that F(Theta_z,-) with all U equal to one is the ordinary z diagram comparison and has z degree zero. Hence M_z(Theta_z)+c_z=0. The relative auxiliary difference and the common WITHIN-z determinant constant then give $\deg_{M_w}F(\Theta_w,-)=0,\qquad \deg_{M_z}F(\Theta_w,-)=-1.$ Similarly F(Theta_z,-) has degrees (-1,0). This is an actual unit-comparison calibration and a relative cap computation. It does not assert equality of the w and z constants or choose them to obtain the answer. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.7 Let a triangle contributing to F(Theta_w,x) have exponents a=n_w and b=n_z and output y. The two homogeneous equalities just proved read Mw(y)-2a=Mw(x) and Mz(y)-2b=Mz(x)-1. Set the intermediate collapsed grading to A=(Mw-Mz)/2. Subtracting gives $A(U^a y)=A(x)+\tfrac12-b.$ Every actual b is nonnegative. Thus after V=1 the chosen type-z band map has Maslov shift zero, algebraic U exponent nonnegative, and Alexander upper shift plus one-half. The type-w map has Maslov shift minus one and Alexander upper shift minus one-half. These statements concern the actual finite triangle counts, including all positive z intersections, not only their associated-graded part. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.8 The NEW arbitrary-old-link split-birth operation supplies an actual triangular matrix [[D,H],[0,D]], with birth the top-column inclusion and death the bottom-row extraction. Its NEW ordinary edge normalization gives H=Da+aD at uniform U and V=1; the explicit degree-zero triangular change Q=[[I,a],[0,I]] conjugates it to diag(D,D) and preserves BOTH those maps. This follows from the actual edge's lower-left coefficient one and the actual weighted index-two chain identity, not a rank inference or an assumed H zero. The two local generators differ by one in BOTH relative Maslov gradings, as the two empty birth bigons show. Thus the ordinary birth map sends the old highest class to the new highest class. With highest origins (n-1)/2 and n/2 its w shift is plus one-half. Death extracts the complementary class one degree below the new highest class and hence has w shift plus one-half as well. Literal w/z exchange gives the SAME two statements for z, using a relative edge from an old z to the new z. Both birth and death therefore have actual pair of degrees (+1/2,+1/2). This uses the proved arbitrary-old-link birth operation, not the earlier same-region auxiliary unlink neck. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.9 For the ACTUAL quasistabilization the new operator at uniform coloring is two copies of D. S-plus uses the w-top generator and S-minus extracts the other generator, so the same highest-class argument gives w shift plus one-half for both. After forgetting w, T-plus uses the z-top and T-minus extracts its complement, so both T maps have z shift plus one-half. The actual relative local difference (1,-1) then gives the full pairs: S-plus and S-minus have (+1/2,-1/2); T-plus and T-minus have (-1/2,+1/2). These conclusions come from actual inclusions, extractions, ordinary top origins and the relative disk index, without declaring an auxiliary absolute half-degree. The H-piece T-plus T-minus accordingly has (-1,+1), agreeing with the actual Psi derivative and its boundary-weighted edge identity. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.10 Every elementary map now calibrated above has EXACTLY the pair in the actual doubled-region Euler ledger: (0,-1) for z saddles, (-1,0) for w saddles, (+1/2,+1/2) for births and deaths, and the respective quasistabilization pairs. The determinant argument supplies homogeneity of the actual counts; the ordinary unit comparisons and literal top/bottom maps supply their constants. Glue the actual movie pieces along m marked intervals. Their region Euler numbers add with subtraction m, precisely canceling the intermediate top origins. The proved doubled-region identity therefore gives the TOTAL pair $(\delta_w,\delta_z)=(\chi(F_w)-(n_0+n_1)/2,\ \chi(F_z)-(n_0+n_1)/2).$ The highest-origin declarations have canceled at every intermediate interface; the endpoint origins are fixed original knot origins. The retained endpoint conjugation/cap interface identifies A=(Mw-Mz)/2 with the ORIGINAL Seifert Alexander normalization, with no correction. Thus for a supplied ACTUAL COMPOSABLE chosen movie, not a merely formal word, the cumulative determinant/endpoint-cap grading is the half-Euler difference. For the constructed genus-g disk-w surface it is (0,-2g), so its full-minus map has Maslov shift zero, nonnegative U exponents and Alexander upper shift g. For a decorated annulus with both regions disks it is (0,0), giving a degree-zero bifiltered map. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra]

1.11 For completeness the relative region Euler ledger is a finite gluing identity. Double a region R across its dividing arcs. At an endpoint with n marked intervals, the corner real boundary frames contribute half of their number. Hence its normalized relative Euler count is chi(R) minus one half of the sum of its incoming and outgoing marked-pair counts. If two pieces glue along m intervals, Euler characteristic subtracts m; the two intermediate half contributions also sum to m. Thus the normalized counts add. Applying this to every actual elementary map calibrated above proves the displayed total pair by induction over the finite chosen movie, with no declaration of an intermediate absolute origin affecting the endpoint total. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $f$ be an orientation-preserving isomorphism of two embedded closed-manifold pointed Heegaard diagrams, carrying their handlebodies, attaching systems and basepoints. Transport $j$, the surface area form, protected sets, and $J_t$ by its surface restriction $\varphi$ and $\Psi=\operatorname{Sym}^g\varphi$.

Then $\Psi$ gives bijections of generators, Whitney classes, their region coefficients, periodic domains and basepoint multiplicities. Postcomposition gives translation-equivariant bijections of the actual finite-energy strip spaces; their geometric linearizations are conjugate by the transported bundle maps, metrics and connections. Consequently actual Fredholm index and regularity agree. Ordinary admissibility in any specified Spin-c sector and full-module admissibility hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other, including sectors with no generators. The global mixed-sign condition corresponds as well.

The actual quotient-count and sum-finiteness conditions are equivalent. Whenever these counts are defined, the generator bijection $f_\#x=\Psi(x)$ intertwines the two hat operators and has the inverse induced by $f^{-1}$. If one operator squares to zero, so does the other, and the two actual diagram chain complexes and homologies are isomorphic. For $g=0$ this is the identity on the empty generator. No analytic existence, comparison between independently selected perturbations, or identity action of an isotopy on homology is asserted.

## Statement references

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual diagram isomorphism and explicitly transported analytic data in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]] specifies the product-torus images, classes, count equation, exact regularity and finiteness conditions, and the two admissibility conventions. It asserts no existence theorem for these counts.

## Proof

1.1 Set $j'=d\varphi j d\varphi^{-1}$, $\eta'=(\varphi^{-1})^*\eta$ and $J_t'=d\Psi J_t d\Psi^{-1}$. The surface map is biholomorphic for the transported structures. The symmetric-product map is smooth with smooth inverse even at repeated tuples: disjoint holomorphic disks around the distinct support points and their transported coordinates give identical elementary symmetric charts. It carries the product-torus images, diagonal and point divisors to their counterparts. The protected integrable sets and constant endpoint collars are transported exactly; tameness holds for the transported descended area form by its defining inequality. Thus the new data are genuinely allowed data, rather than a formal relabeling of counts. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Postcomposition by $\Psi$ carries maps and relative homotopies to maps and homotopies with the same marked ends and transported boundary tori. Its inverse reverses this, so the Whitney classes and generators are bijected. Oriented surface regions and divisor coorientations are preserved, hence all region and basepoint multiplicities agree, and periodic full-curve boundaries correspond. The exact chain rule gives $\partial_s(\Psi u)+J_t'(\Psi u)\partial_t(\Psi u)=d\Psi(u_s+J_t(u)u_t)$. Both directions therefore carry actual solutions. Uniform ends and longitudinal translations are preserved. For the transported metric energy is exactly equal; any other fixed smooth metric on the compact target is uniformly equivalent, so energy finiteness agrees. This proves an actual translation-equivariant bijection. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Transport a connection and metric on the tangent bundle by $\Psi$. Its differential is an isometry on pulled-back bundles and commutes with their covariant derivatives, hence is an isomorphism of the geometric $H^1$ domain and $L^2$ target with their actual boundary subbundles. Differentiate the nonlinear identity of step 2.1 at a zero. The term differentiating $d\Psi$ multiplies the zero nonlinear section and vanishes. Thus $P_{\Psi u}d\Psi=d\Psi P_u$, identifying kernels, ranges and cokernels. Index and surjectivity agree. Equivalently the covariant linearization of the conjugated section is natural with these transported connections on representatives; this also respects the class index wherever that class index is defined. Normalized periodic classes and all formal periodic domains correspond bijectively, as do their coefficients. Push a Spin-c lift forward by the oriented tangent-bundle isomorphism of the diagram transport. Its determinant line is pushed forward as well, and its cap cycles satisfy $H(f_\#P)=f_*H(P)$. The determinant clutch definition of the first Chern pairing therefore gives $\langle c_1(f_\#\mathfrak s),H(f_\#P)\rangle=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle$. This bijects ALL Spin-c structures, even the empty-generator sectors. Consequently the specified-sector Chern-kernel predicate and its full-all-sector version in [F1] correspond, as does the global mixed-sign predicate. This conclusion is not based merely on the indices of realized classes. This argument makes no unproved identification with a Chern-class formula. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Squaring this identity proves the stated square-zero transfer, and the inverse chain maps induce inverse homology maps whenever defined. For $g=0$ all spaces are the point symmetric product and the empty generator gives the claimed identity. These maps are constructed by transport; no step equated them with an identity action for an ambient isotopy or compared independently chosen almost complex paths. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a finite collection of admitted compact marked sutured diagrams, a finite sequence of diagram moves or surface cuts, and finite-dimensional parameter families of dimension at most two. Suppose the local Fredholm, finite-dimensional Sard, compactness and gluing constructions are supplied for their actual Cauchy–Riemann operators, including the prescribed endpoint and protected-neighborhood conditions. All selections needed to apply those constructions, choose coherent determinant orientations, and obtain simultaneous regular data can then be made under Countable Choice. In particular no uncountable choice of analytic charts or regular data is needed for these fixed finite integral Floer constructions.

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[def-countable-choice]] supplies choices from a countable family of nonempty sets. Finite choices require no additional axiom.

[F2] The supplied local operator constructions are used pointwise, not as an assumption that one has already chosen a family over an uncountable index set. Their Fredholm normal forms and finite-dimensional Sard conclusions are part of the hypotheses of this selection lemma.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite admitted geometric data in the statement and their pointwise local analytic constructions.

1.1 A finite surface cellulation gives finitely many regions and finitely many generator tuples. Polygon domains have integer coefficients in that finite region set; periodic groups are subgroups of finite free integer groups and can be given bases by integer row operations. Zero-domain sphere insertions are indexed by integers. Thus all relevant classes, corner tuples, strip/triangle/quadrilateral types and parameter types form a countable set. The compact targets have finite coordinate atlases. Choose rational Sobolev exponents and rational weights in the finitely many endpoint spectral gaps. On compact strip exhaustions, rational piecewise polynomial functions in the coordinate charts, with the prescribed asymptotic references, form countable dense sets in the finite-order Sobolev spaces. The required reference paths between the finite generator sets are finite choices. If reference maps are used separately for homotopy classes, their index set is countable and F1 selects them. These constructions give actual second-countable mapping spaces, rather than an assertion of arbitrary Banach-space separability. [given, construct]

1.2 For almost-complex structures, use a fixed admitted reference and its local Cayley coordinates. Allowed anti-commuting tensor perturbations are supported away from the protected region and satisfy the specified endpoint conditions. Rational coordinate bump functions and rational polynomial tensors on a countable exhaustion of that open support give countable dense subsets. The smooth space has the complete metric obtained by summing 2 to the minus k times the truncated C-to-the-k seminorm distances. The fixed boundary/family-jet conditions define closed affine subspaces of the parameter tensors. Tameness is enforced by working in an open Cayley chart and taking the first closed metric ball strictly inside it. For a family of dimension zero, one or two, take the product with its compact finite-dimensional parameter cube and impose its fixed boundary jets in the same tensor description. No unrestricted product of nonempty sets is used. [step 1.1, construct]

1.3 The universal solution spaces inherit countable bases from these mapping and parameter spaces. Their pointwise Fredholm charts form an open cover. For each basic open set contained in some such chart, choose one chart containing it, with its finite kernel, finite cokernel and finite stabilizing perturbations. This is a countable family of nonempty choices, so F1 applies. The chosen charts cover every solution: every solution has a basic neighborhood inside its pointwise chart. Finite-dimensional bases, cokernel columns and local frames are then chosen only over this countable family. This is the exact place where a casual choice of one chart for every solution would unnecessarily invoke full Choice. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2]

1.4 In one chosen Fredholm normal form the projection to perturbation data is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,g(x,y))$, with $x$ in a Banach space and $y$ in a finite-dimensional kernel coordinate space. Criticality is failure of $D_yg$ to surject onto the finite-dimensional second target factor. Shrink the chart and take a closed product $B\times Q$ contained in its domain, where $B$ is a closed Banach ball and $Q$ is a closed finite-dimensional cube. Its critical-value image is closed relative to the target chart: if $(x_j,g(x_j,y_j))$ converges to $(x,z)$, then $x_j\to x$ because $x_j$ is the FIRST TARGET COORDINATE; no compactness of the Banach ball is used. Compactness of $Q$ gives a subsequence $y_j\to y$, and closedness of $B$ and continuity give $(x,y)\in B\times Q$, $g(x,y)=z$. The nonsurjective finite-dimensional derivative condition is closed, so the limit is critical. Intersect this image with a closed inner target ball lying in the coordinate chart to obtain an exclusion closed in the whole perturbation space. It has empty interior: any target open product has some fixed first coordinate $x$, and finite-dimensional Sard for $y\mapsto g(x,y)$ supplies a second coordinate outside its critical values. Countable-basis centers and rational radii give countably many such domain products and inner target balls covering every chart point and its image. Their critical-value images are thus only countably many closed nowhere-dense exclusions. Taking the union over the countable class and family list remains countable. [F2, step 1.3, construct]

1.5 For smooth perturbations the same exclusions are closed in the stronger smooth topology, and their complements are dense there. Indeed, the local surjectivity directions can be taken smooth and supported in the allowed open region. Their span is finite dimensional. In that span the finite-dimensional Sard perturbation can be made arbitrarily small in any specified finite list of C-to-the-k seminorms; it therefore meets every basic smooth neighborhood. At parameter boundaries the endpoint regularity is already supplied, and gluing collars are fixed; the perturbations act only in the remaining interior. Thus the same countable residual construction applies simultaneously with every prescribed relative condition. [F2, step 1.2, step 1.4]

1.6 Here no appeal to an unrestricted form of the Baire theorem is needed. Enumerate a countable basis of metric balls and enumerate the dense open complements U_n of the exclusions. Having chosen a closed ball B_n, choose the least-index basic ball with positive radius less than 2 to the minus n minus one whose closure lies in the interior of B_n intersected with U_n. Such a ball exists by density and openness. This is recursion on the natural numbers with a unique least-index choice, not a use of Dependent Choice. Its centers form a Cauchy sequence; completeness gives a limit in every B_n, hence in every U_n. Starting with a closed ball inside the permitted Cayley chart keeps the limit tame and preserves the fixed boundary data. The result is one actual simultaneous regular choice for all the fixed problems. [step 1.2, step 1.5, construct]

1.7 For compactness, retain the supplied energy bounds and the actual cap-divisor or basepoint barriers, so every sequence lies in the same compact target region. Index the local elliptic estimates by the countable operator charts, integer energy bounds, integer derivative orders, rational error tolerances and compact strip intervals with integer endpoints. Whenever an estimate needs a constant, take the least integer larger than a valid positive constant. A gradient blow-up center may be taken as the least-index rational grid point where the gradient exceeds half its relevant supremum, and its rescaling factor as a rational within the required factor-two interval. Thus no selection over all points of a limiting curve is needed. On every compact interval and in every derivative order, use the supplied local precompactness and the countable Sobolev bases to extract a subsequence by least-index balls containing infinitely many terms. The diagonal subsequence is indexed by the paired natural-number list of intervals and derivative orders. Its limits are consistent because the subsequences are nested. Bubble and end limits are obtained by this same countable construction; the supplied domain-area identity, positivity and bubble exclusion apply to these actual limits. After the given compactification bounds the number of nonconstant levels, only finitely many breaking levels are retained. This is the complete selection scope of the compactness application, not a new compactness theorem for arbitrary targets. [F2, step 1.1, step 1.3, construct]

1.8 For gluing, use the finite local coordinate covers and the already supplied operator gluing estimates on each broken-curve chart. Work in higher Sobolev Hilbert spaces with the fixed finite-atlas inner products. The inverse on the orthogonal complement of the finite kernel is canonical; for an onto stabilized operator D it is D* times the inverse of DD*. Thus it needs neither a Hahn–Banach extension nor a choice of bases in an arbitrary infinite-dimensional space. The glued approximate inverse is corrected by its convergent Neumann series. Choose the neck threshold as the least integer beyond the valid local estimate, and choose all contraction radii as smaller rational numbers. The correction is the limit of the contraction iterates starting at zero, a specified recursion. The broken-curve spaces have the countable chart covers already constructed in step 1.3; at a bounded compact end a finite subcover supplies a uniform estimate if needed. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $p,q$ be coprime nonzero integers, let $0<r<1$, put $s=\sqrt{1-r^2}$, and let $K(u)=(r e^{ipu},s e^{iqu})$, $u\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$, be the canonically oriented $T(p,q)$. Set $m=|p|$ and $\delta=\pi/(m+1)$. The curves $K$ and $K_\delta(u)=(r e^{ipu},s e^{i(qu+\delta)})$, both oriented by increasing $u$, are disjoint parallel curves on the same Heegaard torus. Their linking number is $pq$. The normal framing of $K$ tangent to this torus has self-linking $pq$. In particular the torus-parallel framing of the canonical positive trefoil $T(2,3)$ has self-linking six. This statement computes the explicit torus framing; it does not identify a particular doubly pointed Heegaard diagram or establish a Floer invariant value.

## Statement references

[[def-coprime-torus-knot]]

[[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]]

[[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Exactly the explicit curves, parameter ranges, signs and orientations in the Statement.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed for the smooth framing and diagram invariance suppliers.

[F1] [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]] uses $\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ in the positive projection plane.

[F2] [[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]] proves that the half-signed mixed-crossing sum is the diagram linking number and is invariant under ambient isotopy, under Countable Choice.

[F3] [[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]] and [[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]] identify a framing's self-linking with that of any sufficiently small parallel push-off in its nonzero normal-section class; the value is unchanged by changing its representative or sufficiently small radius.

[F4] [[def-coprime-torus-knot]] fixes the explicit complex torus curve and orientations used here.

[F5] [[lem-choice-free-isotopy-extension-for-a-compact-smooth-source]] turns a smooth embedding isotopy of a compact source, stationary near its time endpoints, into an ambient isotopy supported near its track.

## Proof

1.1 On the Heegaard torus use angular coordinates $(\theta,v)$. The map $(u,e)\mapsto(r e^{ipu},s e^{i(qu+e)})$ for $0\le e\le\delta$ is an embedded annulus. Indeed an equality of first coordinates gives $u'-u=2\pi k/m$ modulo $2\pi$. Since $p,q$ are coprime, the nonzero residues of $2\pi qk/m$ have distance at least $2\pi/m$ from zero modulo $2\pi$, whereas $|e'-e|\le\delta<2\pi/m$. Equality of second coordinates thus forces $k=0$ and $e=e'$. The two parameter derivatives are independent because $p\ne0$. In particular its two boundary curves are the specified disjoint parallels. [F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Use the orientation-preserving stereographic chart $\Psi(z_1,z_2)=(\operatorname{Re}z_1,\operatorname{Im}z_1,\operatorname{Re}z_2)/(1-\operatorname{Im}z_2)$ and project to its first two coordinates, viewed from positive third coordinate. Its orientation is positive at $(0,0,0,-1)$ and hence everywhere: the boundary-positive tangent basis there is $(\partial_{x_1},\partial_{y_1},\partial_{x_2})$ and its derivative is a positive scalar. In this projection each curve has polar angle $pu$. If its second complex phase is $v$, its radius is $R(v)=r/(1-s\sin v)>0$ and height is $Z(v)=s\cos v/(1-s\sin v)$. The angular derivative is $p\ne0$, so the planar projection is an immersion on both components. [F1, F4, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 A mixed crossing pairs parameters $u$ on $K$ and $u'=u+2\pi k/m$ on $K_\delta$, for exactly one $k\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. Put $v=qu$ and $c_k=2\pi qk/m+\delta$. Equality of radii says $\sin v=\sin(v+c_k)$. Since $\delta$ is strictly between zero and $2\pi/m$, no $c_k$ is zero modulo $2\pi$. The equality therefore holds exactly when $2qu+c_k=\pi$ modulo $2\pi$. For each $k$ this equation has exactly $2|q|$ solutions $u$ modulo $2\pi$. Hence there are exactly $2|pq|$ mixed pairs. At any fixed projected polar angle, the $m$ phases on either component are distinct because $q$ is coprime to $m$, and the phase sets of the two components are disjoint by the same strict bound on $\delta$. A given sine value has at most two distinct phase preimages modulo $2\pi$. Consequently a projected point has at most two preimages in the whole link, so there are no triple points or quadruple coincidences, and the mixed pairs counted are distinct crossings. [step 1.1, step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 At each crossing the two phases are $v$ and $\pi-v$ modulo $2\pi$, with equal denominators and opposite cosines. Their cosines are nonzero, since otherwise these two phases coincide, which would contradict the distinct-phase argument of step 3.1. Write $v_o$ for the phase of the over-strand. Then $\cos v_o>0$, because its height is positive and the other height negative. In the positive radial/angular frame the two oriented tangent vectors are $(a,pR)$ and $(-a,pR)$, where $R=r/(1-s\sin v_o)$ and $a=qrs\cos v_o/(1-s\sin v_o)^2$. Their determinant is $2apR$, nonzero of sign $pq$. The same reasoning applies to self-crossings, because two distinct phases on one component with the same sine are also of this form. The projection is therefore a regular diagram, and all $2|pq|$ mixed crossings have sign $\operatorname{sgn}(pq)$. By [F2] its half-sum is $pq$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, given, algebra]

5.1 The annulus in step 1.1 is generated by the torus vector $\partial_v$, whose image in the normal quotient of $K$ is nowhere zero: $\partial_v$ cannot be a multiple of the tangent $p\partial_\theta+q\partial_v$ because $p\ne0$. This normal class is a torus-tangent framing. Any other nowhere-zero torus-tangent normal section differs by a nowhere-zero real scalar; within its constant sign it is homotopic by positive scalar interpolation, and reversing its sign is homotopic by a constant half-turn in the oriented two-dimensional normal bundle. For small positive $e$, the curve $K_e$ is a push-off in this framing class. This can also be checked in a normalized tubular chart: its normal coordinates divided by $e$ tend uniformly to the nonzero class of $\partial_v$, so the straight interpolation with that class stays nonzero for all sufficiently small $e$. Decreasing $e$ from $\delta$ to a small positive value preserves the annulus's disjoint parallel curves. Make this two-circle family stationary near its time endpoints and apply [F5]; then [F2] and [F3] identify the computed linking number with the framing self-linking. Substituting $p=2,q=3$ gives six. This argument uses the actual finite signed-crossing calculation, not a linking/intersection theorem with a stronger choice hypothesis. [A1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $G,G'$ be knot grids related by exchanging two consecutive columns whose marking-height intervals are disjoint or strictly nested. The same assertion holds for rows, using intervals of marking abscissae, and for a switch, where an $X$ and an $O$ of the exchanged columns share a row. Identify variables by their individual $O$-markings, retaining the full polynomial ring. There are explicit filtered chain maps $P:C^-(G)\to C^-(G')$ and $Q:C^-(G')\to C^-(G)$ given by empty pentagon counts with their $O$-monomial weights, and filtered homotopies $H,H'$ given by empty hexagon counts, satisfying
$$dH+Hd=\operatorname{id}+QP,\qquad d'H'+H'd'=\operatorname{id}+PQ.$$
The maps preserve Maslov grading and do not increase Alexander filtration; the homotopies have Maslov degree $+1$ and do not increase filtration. Taking the associated graded retains precisely the polygons avoiding $X$. Setting all $O$ variables to zero in that associated-graded equivalence gives the tilde equivalence. The maps and homotopies remain valid under any coefficient specialization.

## Statement references

[[def-grid-diagram-for-an-oriented-knot]]

[[alg-grid-knot-floer-complex]]

[[lem-grid-alexander-grading-integral]]

[[lem-grid-rectangle-boundary-square-zero-and-filtration]]

[[lem-grid-rectangle-differential-squares-to-zero]]

[Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, *Grid Homology for Knots and Links*, §§5.1 and 13.3.1](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~petero/GridHomologyBook.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two grids and the individual marking labels specified in the statement. Work over characteristic two.

[F1] [[alg-grid-knot-floer-complex]] counts empty-state rectangles, weights them by the product of variables at their $O$-markings, allows all $X$ in the full filtered version, and excludes $X$ in the associated graded.

[F2] [[lem-grid-alexander-grading-integral]] gives the Maslov rectangle difference $1-2n_O(r)+2\#(\mathbf x\cap\operatorname{Int}r)$ and the Alexander difference $n_X(r)-n_O(r)$.

[F3] [[lem-grid-rectangle-boundary-square-zero-and-filtration]] gives the two decompositions of nonreturning pairs of empty rectangles, including the overlapping four-moving-point case, and identifies returning thin annuli.

[F4] [[lem-grid-rectangle-differential-squares-to-zero]] proves that the full and associated-graded rectangle operators are differentials.

## Proof

1.1 Draw both diagrams on one torus with their markings fixed. Their horizontal circles agree, and all but one vertical circle agree. Denote the different vertical circles by $\beta,\gamma$; draw them crossing transversely at two points $a,b$ away from the horizontal circles, with one marking-bearing bigon on each side. The noninterleaving interval condition allows the two intervening annular regions to avoid all markings: draw $\gamma$ around the two endpoint levels of the exchanged columns, leaving each endpoint marking on its original side. Choose $a$ as the southern tip of the bigon with $\beta$ on its western boundary and $\gamma$ on its eastern boundary; the other tip is $b$. For a switch, the shared-row $O,X$ lie in the same straight-strip region but on opposite sides of the curved circles; the same marking-free intervening annuli remain. [given, construct]

2.1 For states $\mathbf x$ of $G$ and $\mathbf y'$ of $G'$, count embedded disks with five convex corners, four in $\mathbf x\cup\mathbf y'$ and the fifth at $a$, boundary on the combined circles, and horizontal boundary satisfying $\partial(\partial_\alpha p)=\mathbf y'-\mathbf x$. Require that the interior contains no state point, but impose no marking restriction. Define $P(\mathbf x)$ as the sum of the targets with coefficient $U^{O(p)}$. Define $Q$ in the reverse direction using the distinguished corner $b$. Define $H$ on $G$ by the same rule for six-sided embedded disks with four state corners and the other two corners $a,b$; define $H'$ on $G'$ in the same way. A side cannot travel completely around its circle in an embedded polygon, so there are finitely many possible sides, corners, and polygons. These are consequently finite polynomial-module maps. [F1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 To compute their degrees, use the nearest-point correspondence from a $\gamma$ state to a $\beta$ state, replacing just its point on the changed circle. The connecting small triangle $t$ contains no other state coordinate. Expanding the pair-counting formula on the two diagrams gives $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf x')=-1+2n_O(t)$: the self-state terms are equal, the marking-self terms differ by $-1$, and the state-marking cross term differs by $0$ or $-2$ according to which side of the marked level the moved point lies. These are the four choices of side and direction of the triangle. Attaching $t$ on the available side of a pentagon yields a rectangle, so [F2] gives $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y')=-2n_O(p)$ and $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y')=n_X(p)-n_O(p)$ for an empty pentagon. For a hexagon, fill its missing bigon, which contains one $O$ and one $X$, to obtain a rectangle; [F2] then gives $M(\mathbf x)-M(\mathbf y)=-1-2n_O(h)$ and $A(\mathbf x)-A(\mathbf y)=n_X(h)-n_O(h)$. Thus the weighted pentagon maps have degree zero and filtration drop $n_X(p)$, and the weighted hexagon maps have degree $+1$ and filtration drop $n_X(h)$. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Expand $d'P+Pd$, keeping each composite domain and its multiplicities. When four coordinates of the initial state are absent from the terminal state, the rectangle and pentagon have disjoint sets of moving coordinates; commute their order, retaining their supports. This is an involution without fixed points, including when the supports overlap with local multiplicity two. When three coordinates move, cut the composite at its reflex corner in the two possible directions. For multiplicity-one domains this is the ordinary seven-corner region. If a multiplicity is two, the reflex corner is the distinguished corner $a$; following the two possible outgoing edges there again yields exactly the alternate rectangle-pentagon decomposition. Emptiness is preserved, since a forbidden state point in either alternative piece would lie in the interior of an original piece. Thus all these terms pair with the same total $O$-weight. [F1, F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 The remaining possibility in $d'P+Pd$ is that the endpoints differ only on the changed circle. A horizontal thin annulus with a small triangle removed has two decompositions and cancels internally. A vertical thin annulus together with that triangle has one decomposition. There are exactly two such vertical domains: adjoining the marking-free annulus on the western side of the changed circle, or adjoining the marking-free annulus on the eastern side. They have the same initial and terminal states; their difference is the difference of those two marking-free annuli. Their marking multiplicities and therefore their polynomial weights agree. They cancel with each other. These cases exhaust the compositions: the rectangle changes two coordinates and the pentagon changes the coordinate on the replaced circle together with at most one further coordinate, so the number of unmatched coordinates is four, three, or one. Hence $d'P+Pd=0$. Exchanging the roles of the two diagrams proves $dQ+Qd'=0$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.2, algebra]

4.2 Expand $dH+Hd+QP$ and group rectangle-hexagon, hexagon-rectangle, and pentagon-pentagon decompositions by domain. Four moving coordinates give the same commuting pair as in step 3.2. Three moving coordinates give eight-corner domains: either seven convex corners and one reflex corner, or five convex corners and three reflex corners, two of the latter at $a,b$. In the first case cut at the sole reflex corner in its two possible directions. In the second, at two reflex corners the outgoing cut is forced by the boundary orientation; at the remaining one either direction is allowed. The resulting two decompositions are exactly the alternative ordered polygon pairs, with equal weights. This also describes the pair when its two types differ, for example one rectangle-hexagon decomposition and one pentagon-pentagon decomposition. There is no third cut: it would either use a convex corner or leave a nonconvex counted polygon. [F3, step 2.1, construct]

5.1 If the initial and terminal states coincide, a contributing domain is the annular region between the changed circle and a consecutive unchanged vertical circle, with the parts of $\beta,\gamma$ on its boundary retained. Its unique permissible cut depends on the locations of the three relevant state points: the cut gives a rectangle-hexagon, hexagon-rectangle, or pentagon-pentagon pair. The three types occur on the same side of the state-point level where the associated cut can proceed without passing a state point. Exactly one side permits this, so exactly one such domain occurs for every initial state, with one decomposition. It contains no marking, by the marking-free annulus construction in step 1.1. It contributes the initial state with coefficient one. No case with one or two unmatched coordinates remains for an endomorphism of the original grid: a state permutation cannot differ in just one coordinate, and two unmatched coordinates cannot support both distinguished corners with convex polygon ends unless the domain is one of the just listed returning annuli. Consequently $dH+Hd+QP=\operatorname{id}$. The same argument on $G'$ proves the identity for $H'$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.2, construct, algebra]

6.1 Step 3.1 makes all four maps filtered with the claimed degrees; steps 4.1 and 5.1 give the chain and inverse-homotopy identities. On the associated graded, their degree-zero filtration components are exactly the polygons with $n_X=0$. The identities therefore pass to that graded complex. Quotienting its coefficients by all $U_i$ retains exactly the polygons with $n_O=0$ as well and gives the tilde identities. Tensoring any of these map identities with another coefficient module preserves them. Row exchanges are obtained by rotating the construction by $90$ degrees and reversing the horizontal-boundary convention accordingly; the same domain cuts and marking weights apply. This proves every assertion. [F1, F4, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra] ∎
