## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$ be a smooth closed connected oriented three-manifold with $H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$, with a pointed Heegaard diagram whose two complete disk systems each cut its handlebody into one ball. Let $P$ be any integral region domain whose chain boundary is an integral linear combination of the full attaching circles. Then $P=c[\Sigma]$ for an integer $c$. Thus $n_z(P)=0$ implies $P=0$.

In particular the assertion applies to every complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of a rational homology sphere. Such diagrams satisfy the global mixed-sign admissibility condition: there is no nonzero periodic domain with zero basepoint coefficient. No disk-index formula, existence of regular perturbations, or Floer invariance is asserted. The conclusion concerns singly pointed complete cut systems; it does not assert the same constant-domain formula for multipointed disk systems cutting a handlebody into several balls.

## Statement references

[[def-countable-choice]]

[[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual splitting, its specified complete compression disks, $H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$ and the integral region domain. All homology groups used below have rational coefficients.

[F1] [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]] gives exactness for an open two-set cover with any coefficient group; [[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]] identifies deformation retracts.

[F2] [[thm-long-exact-sequence-of-a-pair-in-singular-homology]], [[thm-excision-for-singular-homology]] and [[thm-five-lemma-for-a-morphism-of-long-exact-sequences]] give the relative connector and the annular-neighborhood comparisons. The connector is the boundary of a relative chain.

[F3] [[lem-a-collar-identifies-boundary-local-homology-with-the-pair-fundamental-class]] gives the unique relative orientation class determined by all interior local generator values and its oriented boundary. It works over $\mathbb Q$ without an axiom of choice.

[F4] [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]] supplies smooth collars of the two compact handlebody boundaries under countable choice. They give a two-sided collar of the specified common splitting surface.

## Proof

1.1 Enlarge the interiors of the handlebodies across a thin common collar from [F4]. These two open sets cover $Y$, retract to $U_\alpha,U_\beta$, and their intersection retracts to $\Sigma$. Mayer–Vietoris [F1] has the exact segment $$H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H_1(U_\alpha;\mathbb Q)\oplus H_1(U_\beta;\mathbb Q).$$ Its first term is zero, so the second arrow is injective. Consequently the kernels of the two individual inclusion maps from the surface have zero intersection. This uses the actual rational homology hypothesis, without replacing $Y$ by a three-sphere or invoking a torsion Spin-c assertion. [F1, F4, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 For either complete attaching system write $C$ for the union of its circles. Cutting the surface along them gives a connected compact oriented surface $S$ with two boundary copies of each circle. To see connectedness from the stated disk condition, cut the handlebody along its specified disks. Its boundary is the sphere boundary of the resulting ball. Removing the interiors of the two disk faces for each compression disk leaves exactly $S$. A sphere with finitely many pairwise disjoint open disk interiors removed is connected: connect two retained points by a path on the sphere and replace every excursion through any removed disk by a boundary-circle arc; finitely many small path adjustments in the disk collars give a path avoiding their interiors. There are finitely many disk faces, and each replacement can be made for an entire excursion interval by its first and last intersection. Thus the required cut surface is connected, including the empty-system case. [F4, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 The annular-neighborhood comparison in [F2] identifies $$H_2(\Sigma,C;\mathbb Q)\cong H_2(S,\partial S;\mathbb Q).$$ Explicitly replace $C$ by disjoint thin annuli retracting onto it, using its finite smooth collars in the oriented surface; pair sequences and the five lemma preserve the relative groups. Excise smaller closed middle annuli, and retract the remaining collar pieces onto the boundary copies of the cut surface. These operations are the displayed isomorphism. The group on the right is one-dimensional on $[S,\partial S]$. Here is the needed top-degree calculation from [F3]: the local value of any relative class at an interior point is a rational multiple of the oriented local generator. Those multiples are locally constant, since restricting to a closed coordinate disk makes the class a multiple of that disk's relative orientation class. The disk relative group is $\mathbb Q$: its pair sequence and a cover of its boundary circle by two open arcs give $H_1(S^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ by [F1]; both arcs are contractible, their intersection has two contractible components, and the kernel on $H_0$ is generated by their difference. Connectedness of the interior of $S$ makes all local multiples one rational number $a$. Subtracting $a[S,\partial S]$ has zero restriction at every interior point and is zero by the pointwise uniqueness in [F3]. This proves the claim, also when $S$ is closed. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 The connector from this one-dimensional relative group to $H_1(C;\mathbb Q)$ is zero. Indeed the boundary of its generator is the sum of the oriented boundary circles of $S$ by [F3]; the two copies of each cut circle map back to that circle with opposite orientations and cancel. Exactness of the pair sequence [F2] therefore makes $$H_1(C;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)$$ injective. Its source has one independent rational generator for each attaching circle: finite disjoint unions split the singular chain complex, and the circle computation in step 2.1 gives one copy of $\mathbb Q$ for each circle. Thus a rational linear combination of the full oriented attaching circles which is zero in surface homology has every coefficient zero. This establishes the needed independence without an assumed symplectic basis or an integral surface intersection theorem. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Write $\partial P=c_\alpha+c_\beta$ in full-circle coefficients. This formal region chain supplies a genuine homological boundary on $\Sigma$: take relative orientation chains of its finitely many region closures, separating their corners and rounding them in small vertex disks. Paired edge contributions cancel with the prescribed coefficients; the remaining corner arcs fill in those vertex disks. The connector construction in [F2] and the orientation-boundary statement [F3] consequently give $[c_\alpha]+[c_\beta]=0$ in $H_1(\Sigma;\mathbb Q)$. Each $c_\gamma$ bounds its integral combination of the specified compression disks inside $U_\gamma$. Therefore $[c_\alpha]=-[c_\beta]$ belongs to both kernels in step 1.1 and must be zero. Step 3.1 applied separately to the two complete systems makes every full-circle coefficient in $c_\alpha,c_\beta$ zero. Hence $\partial P=0$ as a region-chain boundary, not just in homology. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Across each curve edge the adjacent region coefficients of $P$ are now equal. The adjacency graph of the regions is connected. [F3] The finite signed cube and its grading are supplied by [[alg-khovanov-chain-complex-from-diagram]], and [[lem-khovanov-cube-differential-squares-to-zero]] proves its differential squares to zero. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Give any actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$ as in [[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], with transverse attaching systems and basepoint $z$. There is a finite sequence of smooth isotopies of individual alpha circles, avoiding $z$ and the other alpha circles, after which opposite systems are again transverse and EVERY nonzero integral periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both positive and negative coefficients. The same splitting surface, manifold, basepoint and beta system are retained; the alpha system still bounds a complete compression-disk system.

Thus globally weakly admissible diagrams can be chosen for every such complete splitting, for general $Y$. Neither a rational homology sphere nor a torsion Spin-c premise is imposed. This is the global condition, stronger than ordinary weakness in ONE specified sector. The input here is an arbitrary complete geometric diagram; it is not asserted to satisfy that condition before the isotopies. The corrected full-module admissibility convention is equivalent to global weakness, whereas a specified-sector-only construction remains separate. No count invariance along the isotopies, sector-index theorem, strong Spin-c admissibility or Floer move map is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual complete diagram and its specified compression disks. A periodic domain here is ANY integral chain of complementary regions with boundary an integral sum of full attaching curves; it need not be known to represent a Whitney class.

[F1] Broad proper auxiliary compression disks admit same-boundary neat replacements with parametrized rounded cut balls by [[lem-proper-compression-disks-admit-neat-witnesses-with-standard-cut-balls]]. For an abstract handlebody apply it after carrying the regular neighborhood of its finite graph to the standard ball-with-handles model embedded in $S^3$, and carry the replacements back. This preparation leaves every attaching circle fixed.

[F2] [[lem-finite-planar-hole-boundary-maps-extend-with-prescribed-collars]] gives actual diffeomorphisms between the finite planar cut surfaces, with all prescribed rim and collar maps.

[F3] [[lem-choice-free-relative-transversality-for-a-compact-smooth-embedding]] supplies arbitrarily small ambient perturbation isotopies of a finite compact circle system transverse to a finite opposite circle system, with support in a prescribed neighborhood. It assumes no stronger choice axiom. Neighborhoods of points disjoint from the moving circles may be excluded from that support.

## Proof

1.1 Prepare either complete disk system by [F1], without changing its boundary. Its one cut ball has a parametrized sphere boundary with two collared disk faces for each attaching circle. Send that punctured sphere by [F2] to a sphere with paired round holes, one pair inside each of finitely many disjoint round cluster disks. Prescribe the map on one rim of each pair arbitrarily with the required orientation and on the other by composing with its actual original pairing, so the map descends across the signed rim collars. Inside each cluster join its two holes by an embedded arc whose endpoints are paired; in the quotient this gives a smooth simple loop meeting just that attaching circle once. The cluster disks are disjoint, so the loops are pairwise disjoint. The signed collars make their intersections transverse. They can avoid $z$: arrange its image outside the finitely many arcs, or move an arc off that one point by a small local detour. Pull back to obtain dual loops for either system. In particular both attaching systems admit loops crossing their individual circles once and missing all other circles of the SAME system. No condition on intersections with the opposite system has yet been imposed. For genus zero there are no curves, and connectedness of the surface already makes every periodic domain constant; the conclusion is immediate. Assume positive genus from now on. [F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Number the original regions and regard real periodic domains with $n_z=0$ as a real subspace $V\subset\mathbb R^r$. It is a rational kernel: subdivide the finite curve graph at its vertices, take the integer matrix sending region coefficients to oriented edge coefficients, require its image to lie in the rational span of full curve vectors, and append $n_z=0$. The coefficients $c_i(P)$ of the alpha circles in $\partial P$ are unique, since full alpha and beta edge vectors have disjoint sets of open edges and each individual circle has an open edge; they are rational linear functions on $V$. The map $c:V\to\mathbb R^g$ is injective. Indeed if its alpha part is zero, $\partial P=\sum_i b_i\beta_i$. Follow the beta-dual loop for $\beta_i$ from step1.1, perturbed to avoid all finite alpha-beta vertices and to cross other curve edges transversely. Across an alpha edge the coefficient jump is zero, and across its sole beta crossing it is $\pm b_i$. The total jump around a closed loop is zero, so $b_i=0$. Thus all boundary jumps vanish. A path on the connected surface joining two region interiors can avoid the finite vertices and cross edges transversely by finitely many small chart detours. It propagates coefficient equality through all regions. Therefore $P$ is constant, and $n_z=0$ makes $P=0$. [step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

3.1 Choose the alpha-dual loops $\gamma_i$ from step1.1 transverse to beta by [F3], keeping them disjoint, avoiding $z$ and retaining their single alpha crossings by making the perturbation small. Choose for each two disjoint parallel copies $\gamma_i^+,\gamma_i^-$, and mutually disjoint annular neighborhoods of all $2g$ copies, avoiding $z$. They meet only $\alpha_i$, in one radial arc. Actual smooth coordinates $(r,\theta)\in(-a,a)\times\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ on each annulus can be chosen with that arc $\theta=0$, by transporting its intersection point around a thin curve collar. Choose $w_i^\pm=(0,\theta_i^\pm)$ with $0<\theta_i^\pm<1$ off beta; there are such points since the central circle is transverse to beta in finitely many points. These points lie off the original curves too. Their region evaluations $n_{w_i^\pm}:V\to\mathbb R$ are rational linear functions. Rational Gaussian elimination and injectivity in step2.1 express each as $\sum_j L_{ij}^\pm c_j(P)$: restrict $c$ to a rational basis of $V$, invert a nonzero maximal minor and extend the resulting left inverse to $\mathbb R^g$. Consequently one finite $C\ge0$ satisfies $|n_{w_i^\pm}(P)|\le C\max_j|c_j(P)|$ for all $P\in V$. If $V=0$ no winding is needed. Otherwise choose an integer $N>C+1$. All this is finite-dimensional linear algebra, with no selection of a basis of an infinite-dimensional space. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix a smooth bump $h(r)$ supported in $(-a,a)$, equal to one near $r=0$, and with $0\le h\le1$. On each plus annulus use the isotopy $H_\tau(r,\theta)=(r,\theta-N\tau h(r))$; on each minus annulus use $(r,\theta+N\tau h(r))$, $0\le\tau\le1$. It is the identity near the annulus boundary and is a diffeomorphism for every $\tau$, with inverse obtained by reversing its angular shift. In particular this is an isotopy of the original circles, not a Dehn twist changing their isotopy classes. The supports are disjoint and meet only their prescribed alpha circle, so the operations can be performed one at a time. Orient the radial arc by increasing $r$ first. Its oriented trace has domain coordinates $(\tau,r)$, boundary the final arc minus the initial arc. At a plus testpoint its preimages solve $-N\tau=\theta_i^+\pmod1$ and there are EXACTLY $N$ solutions in $0<\tau<1$. The Jacobian to $(r,\theta)$ has determinant $+Nh(0)>0$, so each contributes $+1$. On the minus annulus the same computation gives determinant $-Nh(0)<0$ and $N$ preimages. Reversing the arc orientation reverses both trace and the convention for its boundary coefficient. Orient each $\alpha_i$ and its annular coordinate consistently so this calculation gives, for its full trace $T_i$, $$n_{w_i^+}(T_i)=N,\qquad n_{w_i^-}(T_i)=-N.$$ For any point off the two arc banks its multiplicity is explicitly the finite signed count of solutions of $\mp N	au h(r)=	heta\pmod1$; this count is locally constant off those banks and its jumps are the stated boundary. Thus the trace chain is defined even if an intermediate circle is tangent to beta. The trace is zero near $z$. This is a computation of an oriented two-chain multiplicity, including the full integer number of turns. [step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Let $\alpha_i'$ be the final circles before the final transversality perturbation. Their trace satisfies $\partial T_i=\alpha_i'-\alpha_i$. For a periodic domain $P\in V$, set $P'=P+\sum_i c_i(P)T_i$. This is an actual integer region chain when $P$ is integral: the trace's integer local degrees are constant away from the old and new alpha arcs; their boundary jumps are exactly the specified trace boundary. The old alpha jumps cancel in the displayed sum. Thus $\partial P'=\sum_i c_i(P)\alpha_i'+\sum_i b_i(P)\beta_i$, and $n_z(P')=0$. Reversing the isotopy gives the inverse chain operation, so ALL normalized periodic domains of the new system occur this way, with the same full-circle coefficients. At the selected points the supports are disjoint, hence $$n_{w_i^\pm}(P')=n_{w_i^\pm}(P)\pm Nc_i(P).$$ If $P\ne0$, pick an index with $|c_i(P)|=\max_j|c_j(P)|>0$. Step3.1 bounds the two old coefficients by $C|c_i(P)|$, strictly less than $N|c_i(P)|$. Thus these two new coefficients have opposite signs. This works for EVERY real nonzero periodic domain and therefore for every integral one, with one single finite $N$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 The winding may leave tangencies to beta. The final circles miss the finitely many selected testpoints: on the center of each annulus $h=1$ and $N$ is integral, so their intersection there is still at $\theta=0$. Choose small closed testpoint neighborhoods missing all final alpha circles and $z$. Apply [F3] successively to each alpha circle, with arbitrarily small supports excluding those neighborhoods and $z$ and disjoint from all other alpha circles. Compact separation retains disjointness and previous transverse intersections. These final small isotopy traces have zero multiplicity at every testpoint and at $z$, so the inverse-trace bijection of step5.1 preserves its exact sign witnesses. Opposite systems are now transverse, and their intersections are finite by compactness and local transversality. Each surface isotopy of an alpha circle extends over its handlebody by a thin boundary collar: if $K_\tau$ is its supported surface ambient isotopy, the collar map $(p,r)\mapsto(K_{\chi(r)}p,r)$ is a diffeomorphism, identity near its inner boundary, with slice-wise inverse and a triangular derivative. Transport its complete disk system by this map. Thus the manifold and splitting did not change, and the resulting alpha curves still bound a complete system. The basepoint and beta curves never moved. Genus zero and $V=0$ were already included. The claimed global admissibility follows, without a Spin-c, analytic count or move-invariance inference. [F3, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a globally weakly admissible complete singly pointed diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, with one surface complex structure $j$, area form and protected nearly symmetric geometry. Use a small Cayley coefficient ball about the standard background, with common exact product generator charts. Let $J^-_t,J^+_t$ be two paths in that ball, constant on genuine endpoint time collars with the same endpoint values as the background. Suppose EVERY nonconstant zero-basepoint strip for either path is regular, in the actual fixed-end $H^1\to L^2$ realization. These are hypotheses about actual chosen data; no Spin-c or rational homology restriction is imposed.

There is a smooth source-dependent path $K(s,t)$ in the same protected coefficient neighborhood, equal to $J^-_t$ for all sufficiently negative $s$ and to $J^+_t$ for all sufficiently positive $s$, constant on genuine positive time collars at $t=0,1$, with the following properties. EVERY actual nonconstant finite-energy solution with uniform generator ends of
$$u_s+K(s,t,u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,0)\in T_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in T_\beta,\qquad n_z(u)=0$$
has onto actual fixed-end operator, in every integer higher realization. Its constant solutions are the generator maps and have invertible index-zero operators. Across all endpoints and realized classes there are finitely many actual index-zero solutions. They are counted WITHOUT a translation quotient: the source transition is fixed. Thus their mod-two numbers define a finite matrix from the $J^-$ generator module to the $J^+$ generator module.

More generally, ANY fixed compact-transition structure in this same family, with these end paths and regular at EVERY zero-basepoint solution, has a finite actual index-zero solution set, by the same anchored argument. The construction proves that such choices exist.

This is regularity and finite continuation counts, not yet a chain-map, composition or chain-equivalence theorem. It compares only the specified common integrable background and protected small family. Changing $j$, comparing merely sector-admissible inputs, Heegaard moves, gradings and plus/infinity maps remain separate. Genus zero gives only the point solution and its identity one-by-one count matrix.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The globally weak complete diagram, common small protected Cayley family and exact charts, and the actual all-zero-basepoint regular end paths.

[F1] The general closed-manifold chosen-complex proof gives the finite rational-kernel domain argument, repeated below independently of an index. Region multiplicities are nonnegative at the protected integrable divisors, and the ordered-lift energy estimate uses only pointwise tameness and the fixed integrable neighborhoods. ([[thm-globally-weak-closed-heegaard-data-admit-a-finite-chosen-hat-complex]], [[lem-pointed-heegaard-integrable-divisor-positivity]], [[lem-nearly-symmetric-heegaard-strip-domain-energy-bound]])

Its hypotheses allow rapidly decaying source perturbations and their compact-transition truncations. ([[lem-asymptotically-autonomous-zero-marked-strips-have-anchored-breaking-compactness]])

[F3] Countable projected matrix bumps and rapid Hilbert weights give smooth Cayley families and tangent density. Boundary-preserving local additions, weak traces and Sobolev algebra give the actual $H^3\cap X_0$ configuration charts and $H^2$ section. The source-dependent coefficient details are supplied below. ([[lem-separable-hilbert-smooth-almost-complex-strip-variations]], [[lem-boundary-preserving-local-addition-for-transverse-product-tori]], [[lem-countable-choice-weighted-strip-sobolev-algebra-and-composition]], [[lem-higher-sobolev-strip-map-charts-and-cauchy-riemann-section]])

## Proof

1.1 In genus zero all maps go to a point and the stated conclusion is direct, so suppose the genus is positive. There is ONE energy bound $B$ for every actual zero-basepoint strip considered here, independent of its index and of its prescribed source dependence in the fixed small coefficient family. To see the domain assertion explicitly, let $L$ be the finite rational kernel of real periodic region chains with $n_z=0$. A nonzero nonnegative vector in it gives a rational such vector by approximation on its positive-coordinate face, and clearing denominators contradicts global admissibility. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Write the two end paths in the common small Cayley coordinates as $J^\pm=J_b(I+C^\pm)(I-C^\pm)^{-1}$. 4.1 This is onto in the actual higher section as well. The low operator has a finite-dimensional cokernel; lift its quotient basis by finitely many parameter directions using step3.1, and solve the remaining range with the bounded inverse on its orthogonal kernel complement. 5.1 Approximate this chosen auxiliary structure by actual compact-transition, time-collar structures. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Give an actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, with transverse attaching systems, one-ball compression cuts, basepoint $z$, a reference orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure and a positive area form. Suppose it is GLOBALLY weakly admissible: every nonzero periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. Broad smooth tangencies of auxiliary compression-disk witnesses are permitted.

There is a choice of surface complex structure, protected region and marked-divisor neighborhoods, common product-integrable generator charts and a nearly symmetric tame path constant on genuine endpoint time collars, for which EVERY nonconstant finite-energy strip with $n_z=0$ has onto actual fixed-end Cauchy--Riemann operator. There are finitely many actual index-one strip orbits with $n_z=0$, across all endpoints and Whitney classes, and their modulo-two count matrix satisfies $\widehat\partial^2=0$. These actual chosen counts therefore define a finite chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$.

Every complete pointed splitting can first be made globally weakly admissible by the finite basepoint-avoiding curve isotopies in [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]]. Consequently a chosen-data complex of this kind can be obtained from every supplied complete splitting of general $Y$. This does not identify complexes before and after those isotopies. The corrected full single-diagram admissibility convention is equivalent to this global condition by its actual zero-Chern-sector supplier. The construction for ONE specified merely sector-admissible input remains a separate result; no generator-only admissibility test is used. Auxiliary-choice and Heegaard-move invariance, Spin-c decomposition, relative or absolute grading, plus/infinity and cobordism maps remain separate. In genus zero the empty generator gives the one-dimensional complex with zero differential; a possibly empty positive-genus generator set is not asserted to have nonzero homology.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual complete singly pointed splitting, its global mixed-sign admissibility, reference complex structure, positive area form and basepoint. No homology or Spin-c restriction on $Y$ is assumed.

[F1] Proper compression disks have same-boundary neat replacements and smooth cut-ball parametrizations after transporting an abstract handlebody to its standard embedded model. These data supply an actual finite oriented surface polygon. A prescribed positive local surface germ extends to a supported disk diffeomorphism with identity boundary collar. ([[lem-proper-compression-disks-admit-neat-witnesses-with-standard-cut-balls]], [[lem-neat-balanced-handlebody-cuts-supply-finite-surface-polygons]], [[lem-smooth-jordan-disk-boundary-maps-extend-to-diffeomorphisms]])

[F2] The rational finite-region proof of [[lem-pointed-heegaard-admissibility-finite-domain-slices]] uses only a rational periodic-domain matrix, the zero-mark mixed-sign property and fixed endpoint corners. Its finite-dimensional argument is repeated explicitly below for these general closed data. [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]] supplies the actual basepoint-avoiding global admissibility isotopies when they are needed.

[F3] Continuous classes admit actual smooth fixed-end models, with homotopy-invariant additive actual index and additive point-divisor degrees. Differences of same-end smooth domains are full-curve periodic; equal domains give equal actual indices, with the supplied finite surface polygon. ([[lem-continuous-whitney-classes-admit-relative-smooth-fixed-end-models]], [[lem-smooth-relative-whitney-homotopies-preserve-strip-fredholm-index]], [[lem-symmetric-product-divisor-intersections-and-point-movement]], [[lem-equal-whitney-domains-have-equal-boundary-windings-and-fredholm-index]])

[F4] Protected point-divisor multiplicities are nonnegative by [[lem-pointed-heegaard-integrable-divisor-positivity]]. The domain-energy estimate is $E(u)\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta$, with one common $C$ on a sufficiently small fixed protected coefficient family. Auxiliary flat-endpoint-jet all-strip regular paths have actual constant-collar approximants regular on EVERY nonconstant zero-marked strip below any specified finite energy bound. The compact cut systems must each have a chosen zero mark in every cut component; here the single basepoint does so. ([[lem-nearly-symmetric-heegaard-strip-domain-energy-bound]], [[thm-countable-choice-flat-endpoint-jet-universal-strip-regularity]], [[lem-zero-marked-bounded-energy-strip-regularity-survives-collar-approximation]])

[F5] For a path regular on all zero-marked strips below $E_*$, the actual index-one orbits below that energy are finite. For each fixed zero-marked index-two class $\phi$, if $E_*>B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta$, the actual compactified one-manifold has finitely many broken rigid ends and gives their modulo-two cancellation. These results apply to general compact Heegaard data, without a torsion Spin-c or knot premise. ([[thm-finite-zero-marked-actual-index-one-strip-counts-under-an-energy-bound]], [[thm-fixed-zero-marked-whitney-class-index-two-compactification-and-mod-two-cancellation]])

## Proof

1.1 If the genus is zero, the target is a point and the stated one-generator zero differential follows directly; assume henceforth positive genus. Prepare the geometric data without a category narrowing. View either actual handlebody as an abstract regular neighborhood of its finite graph, transport it to the standard ball-with-handles model embedded in $S^3$, apply [F1]'s broad same-boundary compression preparation there and transport back. The surface, attaching circles and diagram in $Y$ are unchanged. The resulting one-ball cut supplies the actual finite polygon needed by [F3]. To choose genuine integrable crossing charts, at each of finitely many crossings take a positive smooth chart $\Psi$ straightening the two arcs and an old holomorphic chart $c$. The positive local germ $c^{-1}\Psi$ fixes that crossing. Extend it by [F1] to a diffeomorphism supported in a small crossing disk, identity near its boundary. Choose these disks disjoint and off all chosen region points and $z$. Their finite composite $F$ gives the actual integrable structure $j=F^*j_{\mathrm{ref}}$; the charts $cF=\Psi$ are holomorphic, with unchanged holomorphic transition maps. Their products give common $\mathbb R^h/i\mathbb R^h$ generator charts in $\operatorname{Sym}^h\Sigma$. Choose protected diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods separated from the two compact tori and smaller generator charts, and use the constant standard background path. No interpolation of surface complex structures has been presumed integrable. [F1, F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Prove domain finiteness independently of an index bound and BEFORE choosing regular counts. Number the regions and let $L\subset\mathbb R^r$ consist of real periodic chains with $n_z=0$. The finite integer boundary matrix, modulo the full-circle span, makes $L$ a rational linear kernel. It contains no nonzero nonnegative vector: if $v\ge0$ were nonzero, restrict to the face of its strictly positive coordinates. A rational basis of that restricted kernel and sufficiently close rational approximations to the finitely many coefficients of $v$ give a nonzero rational nonnegative vector. Clearing denominators contradicts the assumed integral mixed-sign condition. Fix endpoints $x,y$ and collect the nonnegative domains of ALL continuous zero-basepoint Whitney classes between them. If the collection is nonempty, choose one domain $D_0$. Differences have their endpoint corners cancel by [F3], so the collection lies in $(D_0+L)\cap\mathbb R^r_{\ge0}$. Its integral members are bounded: otherwise choose, using a fixed enumeration of $\mathbb Z^r$, integral members of norm exceeding each integer. Normalize them. A subsequence has a nonnegative unit-vector limit, by successive subdivision of the finite coordinate cube and retention of the first subcube containing infinitely many indices. Its difference from $D_0/\|D_n\|$ lies in the closed kernel $L$, so the limit is a forbidden nonzero nonnegative member of $L$. Thus there are only finitely many integral domains for this pair. This is the actual [F2] argument, requiring no rational-homology-sphere premise. [F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Take the finite union $\mathcal D$ of these finite sets over the finite generator pairs. Let $C$ be a common domain-energy constant on the small protected coefficient family in [F4] and put $$B=\max\left(\{C\sum_R n_R(D)\int_R\eta:D\in\mathcal D\}\cup\{0\}\right),\qquad E_*=B+1.$$ Every actual zero-basepoint holomorphic strip has a nonnegative region domain, by protected-divisor positivity, hence has energy at most $B$ by [F4]. More importantly, any concatenation of two such strips has a nonnegative domain, zero basepoint degree and a continuous Whitney class by [F3]; its domain is itself in $\mathcal D$. Its fixed-class bound $B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta$ is therefore at most $B$ too. This uniform bound uses all continuous nonnegative domains, not just eventually counted strips. There is no claim that two classes with the same domain are equal, or that all signed domains are bounded. [F3, F4, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Use the zero-mark set consisting ONLY of $z$; the additional protected region divisors are not required to have zero degree. Choose in this protected family an auxiliary all-strip regular flat-jet path from [F4]. Its genuine constant-collar approximants have the same surface, boundary structures, generator charts and common energy constant. The bounded-energy zero-marked openness theorem in [F4] makes every sufficiently late approximant regular on every nonconstant zero-basepoint strip of energy at most $E_*$. Fix one. Step 3.1 bounds ALL of its actual zero-basepoint strips by $B<E_*$, so it is regular for all of them, including every possible limiting level; no negative-index nonregular level is left uncontrolled. This also implies each nonconstant such strip has positive actual index, since its nonzero longitudinal derivative is a square-integrable kernel section by its exact end decay and onto-ness. Applying the actual finite-count assertion in [F5] now gives finitely many index-one orbits across every generator pair and represented class. Their modulo-two finite sums define a matrix on the finite vector space. [F4, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Fix initial and final generators. A term in the coefficient of their differential square is an ordered pair of these finitely many rigid orbits. Its concatenated continuous class $\phi$ has zero basepoint degree and actual index two by [F3]. There are only finitely many such ordered pairs and hence finitely many such concatenated classes; distinct classes with identical domains are not identified. For EACH of these actual classes step 3.1 gives $B_\phi\le B<E_*$. The chosen path is regular on its entire required zero-basepoint energy range by step 4.1, so [F5]'s fixed-class compactification and parity theorem apply. Its boundary pairs are exactly all the rigid orbit pairs whose concatenated class is this $\phi$. Their number is even. Summing this identity over the finite list of actual concatenated classes exhausts the coefficient of the differential square and makes it zero in $\mathbb F_2$. No summation over merely formal domains, no finiteness assumption for arbitrary class sets, and no positive-mark boundary-degeneration theorem were used. [F3, F5, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 If the supplied complete splitting is not globally weakly admissible, first apply [F2]'s winding theorem. It leaves $Y$, the splitting surface and basepoint fixed, retains complete disk systems and ends with transverse curves satisfying exactly the global hypothesis used in step 2.1. The preceding construction applies to that diagram. No chain map comparing its counts to counts on the original diagram has been supplied by the winding theorem or by this proof. In particular the conclusion is existence of an actual finite chosen-data complex for general closed $Y$, not its topological invariance, a construction for every weaker sector-admissible input, or a grading assertion. Genus zero was settled in step 1.1; the empty-set cases in steps 2.1 and 3.1 give $B=0$ and a finite zero module if no positive-genus generators exist. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Suppose two complete globally weak pointed Heegaard diagrams for any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold differ by a supplied attaching-circle isotopy avoiding the basepoint and the other circles of its own family. Their actual chosen hat complexes, with the auxiliary choices described below, have actual finite chain maps and inverse chain homotopies. The construction uses diagram transport on regular intervals and genuine triangle maps at finitely many births and deaths. The local inverse at a birth is an explicit unit-pair cancellation map composed with a finite action-triangular inverse. It does not assume that birth cancellation preserves counts or that arbitrary intermediate diagrams are admissible.

One fixed finite winding preparation makes the whole central isotopy globally weak. The preparation and its removal are themselves globally weak isotopies. All finite analytic comparisons are performed using the stated continuation suppliers and consistently retained actual generator charts. This proves the attaching-circle isotopy operation between globally weak hat diagrams for general Y, including both attaching families. It does not prove the sector-only input comparison, positive-basepoint minus invariance, absolute grading or naturality.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The compact supplied smooth circle isotopy, globally weak endpoint diagrams and Countable Choice. Its own-family circles remain disjoint and its basepoint remains avoided.

[F1] The finite winding proof constructs disjoint paired dual-loop annuli for either complete system, computes their actual signed winding traces as $\pm N$, and proves the inverse-trace bijection on ALL periodic domains and injectivity of their boundary coefficients. ([[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]])

[F2] Smooth Sard holds in finite dimensions under Countable Choice. ([[thm-morse-sard-for-smooth-manifolds]])

[F3] Actual transported diagram data give literal inverse chain isomorphisms; no isotopy acts as the identity by assumption. ([[lem-closed-pointed-diagram-isomorphisms-identify-hat-counts]])

[F4] Actual small bigons have count one and a bounded phase-fixed inverse. Actual embedded triangles have index zero, bounded inverse and count one, also under small regular protected perturbations. The small-isotopy finite-action argument and its bounded-density area choice are proved in the handleslide operation. ([[lem-circular-handleslide-top-triangles-have-actual-count-one]], [[thm-globally-weak-hat-handleslides-have-explicit-inverse-homotopies]])

[F5] Coherent all-index regular zero-mark polygon data and actual finite triangle chain maps exist on the globally weak multidiagrams. Their pair differential squares to zero. The supplied full-boundary and changing-background continuations give the stated actual auxiliary chain equivalences, first aligning the two boundary tensors at their own fixed backgrounds and then comparing backgrounds with that common boundary tensor. ([[thm-globally-weak-multidiagrams-admit-coherent-all-index-regular-polygon-data]], [[thm-globally-weak-zero-marked-polygons-have-finite-counts-and-a-infinity-boundaries]], [[thm-changing-complex-background-zero-marked-continuations-are-chain-equivalences]], [[thm-fixed-symmetric-background-hat-complexes-with-different-boundary-values-are-equivalent]])

## Proof

1.1 Make the compact isotopy generic by an actual finite-dimensional perturbation relative its endpoint collars and marked-point neighborhoods. In finitely many graph charts write intersection with the fixed opposite curve as $f(t,\theta)=0$. Take finite chart bump functions and their coordinate products to embed the compact parameterized circles: a positive bump identifies its local chart, its coordinate products recover the point, and their differentials recover each tangent vector. These finitely many functions, together with polynomials through degree five in those coordinates and finite chart cutoffs, separates two-jets at each point and one-jets at any two distinct points: at two distinct embedded coordinate vectors choose a linear function taking distinct values and multiply its cubic interpolation factors by the local degree-two monomials. The conditions $f=f_\theta=0$ are therefore transverse on the two-dimensional parameter cylinder. The three conditions adding either $f_t=0$ or $f_{\theta\theta}=0$ are excluded, and the simultaneous two-point tangency condition has four equations on the three-dimensional configuration $(t,\theta,\theta')$, so is excluded as well. Apply [F2] on its countably many coordinate patches and take one common arbitrarily small perturbation. Compactness makes the tangency set finite, with distinct event times. Smallness retains the actual embedded circle family, its own-family disjointness and its avoided marks. Taylor expansion and the scalar parameter Morse completion give exactly the local ordinary fold $y=x^2-t$. [F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Prepare one uniformly admissible movie, rather than assuming all the original intermediate diagrams are admissible. Wind the FIXED opposite system using [F1]. Its paired dual loops can avoid the finite region representatives at BOTH endpoints. Choose the winding test points in open central plateaus of those annuli, away from the endpoints and common regular values of all the finitely many compact moving-curve trace maps $(t,\theta)\mapsto\Sigma$. Sard [F2] supplies such points. Their trace preimages are finite, so the multiplicities of every partial moving trace there are bounded by one finite integer K, uniformly in t. Homology relations among full circles remain constant along the isotopy. Since each complete family has independent homology classes, the moving boundary coefficients are rational linear functions of the fixed-system boundary coefficients, on their relation space; use a nonzero maximal minor. The original periodic evaluations are likewise bounded linear functions of these fixed coefficients by [F1]'s injectivity. Thus one finite C bounds every intermediate test evaluation by C times the maximum fixed boundary coefficient. At a time when a moving curve passes a test point use the two one-sided region evaluations; the extra jump is bounded by the same coefficient norm. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Take one integer $N>C+1$. The exact opposite winding traces of [F1] add $+Nb_i$ and $-Nb_i$ to the paired evaluations of every periodic domain, where $b_i$ is its fixed-system boundary coefficient. A nonzero domain has some $|b_i|$ maximal and positive, so the two resulting evaluations have opposite signs, uniformly along the WHOLE central path. If a selected point lies momentarily on a moving curve, sufficiently close one-sided points give the same strict signs. Hence the wound central movie is globally weak at every regular slice. The winding paths at the two ends are globally weak too: their supports avoid the selected old region representatives, so the inverse-trace correspondence leaves ALL their old coefficients unchanged at those points during EVERY partial winding. Nonnegativity would give an old nonnegative periodic domain, hence zero, and the inverse trace then makes the new one zero. Finally perturb the finite movies generically while retaining these open sign neighborhoods. The original endpoints are thus joined by winding, the uniformly weak central path and unwinding, all with finitely many ordinary events. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 On a closed interval containing no event, transverse intersection paths are smooth. Construct a compact surface vector field carrying the moving curves and preserving the fixed opposite curves SETWISE. At an intersection add a tangential velocity along the moving curve so that its total velocity is tangent to the fixed curve; transversality gives a unique scalar adjustment. In its local transverse axes extend that common prescribed value by compatible smooth fields tangent to the fixed axis and with the required normal component on the moving axis. Outside these finitely many patches use ordinary curve collars; a finite partition retains both linear conditions. The compact flow fixes the marks and transports both actual systems. By [F3] it gives an actual chain isomorphism with inverse for transported data. This proves the regular-interval operation without presuming that its action on homology is the identity. [F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

4.2 At one birth use the scalar normal form $y=x^2-t$ in a disk containing no other intersections or marks. The positive change of horizontal coordinate $x\mapsto x\sqrt{2R-x^2}$, with R fixed and the patch small, sends the parabola to the lower circle arc $y=R-\sqrt{R^2-x^2}-t$, while keeping horizontal lines horizontal. Use this circular-cap representative for the actual local complex model. A sufficiently small Hamiltonian displacement of the opposite horizontal arc crosses that cap once and creates exactly the same two new intersections. Its compensating zero-mean displacement can be supported in a second collar arc missing the moving family. The endpoint representatives are joined to those of the given fold by regular-interval isotopies, since no further tangency occurs after shrinking the two parameter intervals. Choose a positive area form annihilating all old periodic domains by the finite-simplex construction in [F4], and balance the small opposite-system displacement for this form. The old/new triple is globally weak: its periodic chains are old chains plus signed thin annuli; retained old-region points first kill the old part, and the two private lune signs kill each remaining coefficient. Thus [F5] supplies actual finite triangle maps and actual square-zero differentials for this local comparison. [F4, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 One surface tangency can create several generator pairs. Enumerate the finitely many complementary matchings by $r=1,\ldots,k$; write their new generators $a_r,b_r$, with the positive small bigon directed $a_r\to b_r$. The remaining coordinates agree in that pair. A strip supported entirely in the thin comparison collar is this small bigon with constant other roots: every other component of the moving curves in that collar has only one old crossing, so has no nonconstant two-ended root. For an index-one strip the local root has degree one by the scalar index computation in [F4]; its other roots are constant. Thus EVERY other strip contributing to the differential contains a fixed old-region core. Choose its area lower bound $c>0$, and take the birth small enough that all small-bigon areas $\delta_r$ and all nearest-triangle areas are below $c/(10\cdot2^{k+1})$. The bounded-density choice in [F4] makes this possible without shrinking c. The actual coefficient $a_r\to b_r$ is one; every other such domain would have the same tiny area, since periodic areas vanish, and could not contain that core. Its reverse and its diagonal coefficients vanish by negative or zero area. These assertions persist for small regular protected perturbations by the actual inverse and zero-mark compactness. Nonlocal entries between DIFFERENT pairs are retained rather than set to zero. [F4, F5, step 4.2, construct, algebra]

6.1 Here is the actual one-pair algebra, applied while the other pairs remain in the complementary vector space O. If the chosen coefficient is one, its reverse and both diagonal coefficients are zero, write the CURRENT finite differential as $$do=Ao+a\lambda(o)+b\mu(o),\qquad da=u+b,\qquad db=v.$$ The equality $d^2=0$ gives $\mu(u)=\lambda(u)=0$, $Au=v$, and $\mu A=\lambda$. Put $D=A+u\mu$ on O, and set $$p(o)=o,\quad p(a)=0,\quad p(b)=u;\qquad i(o)=o+a\mu(o);\qquad h(b)=a,\quad h(a)=h(o)=0.$$ Direct multiplication gives $D^2=0$, $pd=Dp$, $di=iD$, $pi=I$, and $$ip+I=dh+hd.$$ On b the last equality is $u+b=da$, on a it is $a=h(u+b)$, and on O it is $a\mu(o)=hdo$. This identity concerns actual finite matrices and does not require the other new generators to be absent. [F5, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 Cancel the pairs successively using step 6.1. Its formula $D=A+u\mu$ expresses each new coefficient as a finite sum of directed paths of ORIGINAL differential entries, with one subtraction of the small-bigon area for each eliminated pair. Paths may revisit an earlier eliminated pair, so count these occurrences: each cancellation concatenates two previous paths and adds one reversed unit edge. Starting with zero such edges, after j cancellations there are at most $2^j-1$. Thus every coefficient path subtracts at most $(2^k-1)\max\delta_r$. A path which uses only local small bigons cannot pass between distinct pairs. Hence every correction to a remaining pair coefficient, its reverse or its diagonal includes a nonlocal original entry of area at least c. Its total area is at least $c-2^{k+1}\max\delta_r>c/2$. Areas telescope along the path, since the original periodic areas vanish. Such a correction cannot have the required area $\delta_s$, $-\delta_s$ or zero. Thus each remaining unit coefficient stays one and its reverse and diagonal coefficients stay zero. This proves inductively that ALL k cancellations are defined. Denote their composite projection and inclusion by P and I, and their final differential on the OLD generator space by D. Composing the displayed single-pair homotopies gives an actual finite K with $$PI=I_{\mathrm{old}},\qquad IP+I_{\mathrm{new}}=dK+Kd.$$ For two cancellations the homotopy is $h_1+i_1h_2p_1$; finite induction proves the formula. No block of nonlocal inter-pair entries has been discarded. [F4, F5, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 Let H be the actual small-isotopy triangle map from the original old complex to the new one, with its two-lune top cycle. It is a chain map by [F5]. Set $T=PH$. Its nearest old-generator coefficient is one by [F4]'s actual triangle inverse. A triangle to ANY $b_r$ cannot stay in the thin opposite-system collar: the isolated tangent component has no old crossing, whereas every other moving-curve collar component has only its one old crossing. It therefore contains an old-region core, as does every other nonnearest direct old-output triangle. Every additional term in PH is a path of such a triangle and original positive strips, subtracting at most $2^{k+1}$ small-bigon areas (the same two-path recurrence bounds the composite projection). It still has core cost at least $c-2^{k+1}\max\delta_r>c/2$; nearest triangles have smaller area. Old periodic areas vanish, so these differences define relative action on each finite old connectivity component. More explicitly any cycle of nonnearest transitions, closed by the reverse nearest triangles, would be a normalized periodic domain of strictly positive area, contrary to the chosen zero periodic areas. Therefore $T=I_0+N$, where $I_0$ is the nearest-generator bijection and $I_0^{-1}N$ is strictly action triangular on a finite set. The finite geometric series is a literal chain inverse of T. This proves the needed assertion after ALL cancellations, not merely one surface pair. [F4, F5, step 4.2, step 5.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

9.1 The actual triangle map H now has explicit inverse $T^{-1}P$. Its left composite is literally the identity. Put $X=HT^{-1}P$ on the new complex. Then $PX=P$; using step 7.1 gives $$X+I=d(KX+K)+(KX+K)d.$$ Indeed $(IP+I)X+(IP+I)=X+I$, since $IPX=IP$. This proves both inverse assertions with every complementary matching included. A death uses the inverse maps and homotopies. All sums, cancellations and inverses are finite actual count matrices; no moving-boundary compactification has been substituted for the calculation. [step 7.1, step 8.1, construct, algebra]

10.1 The finite concatenation can be made with actual analytic comparisons satisfying their stated hypotheses. First fix all local geometric intervals and their finitely many balanced area forms. At each regular interval transport the actual generator charts by the flow of step 4.1. ## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] A complete globally weak diagram admits actual regular finite zero-basepoint data and a square-zero chosen hat differential. The actual count convention uses index one before longitudinal translation. ([[thm-globally-weak-closed-heegaard-data-admit-a-finite-chosen-hat-complex]], [[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]])

[F2] The point-divisor line and its relative degree are constructed even at repeated tuples. Moving the point inside one attaching-complement component preserves its relative degree. ## Proof

**Given:** The actual globally weak diagram, chosen regular hat data and Countable Choice.

Subtract that intersection and call the lifted holomorphic strip W. Its boundary values lie in $\mathbb R,i\mathbb R$ and tend to zero at both ends. Finite energy thus makes $W\in H^1$. Conjugate reflection across $t=0$ and negative-conjugate reflection across $t=1$ give an $H^1$ extension, antiperiodic with period two. Even-kernel convolution followed by real longitudinal cutoffs supplies smooth approximants with the same two boundary planes. Thus W belongs to precisely the boundary completion in [F4]. The actual inverse [F4] applied to $D_0W=0$ makes W zero. [F4, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

6.2 Check global weak admissibility, rather than assuming it is preserved. Each new meridian has the SAME connected z-region on its two sides; that region was described in step 5.1. Every region two-chain is consequently the old coefficient vector with that one region replaced by its joined counterpart. For a periodic new chain, the coefficient jump across the new meridians is zero, so its boundary coefficient on each new full circle is zero. Across old edges its jumps and boundary condition are the old ones. Restriction therefore identifies its periodic domains with the old periodic domains, preserving every old coefficient and $n_z$. Conversely each old periodic chain extends with that same region coefficient, and is periodic. A nonzero normalized chain thus has both signs by the old global weakness. This proves the NEW diagram is globally weakly admissible, with no periodic-index or Spin-c formula assumed. [F1, step 1.2, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 Conversely every old zero-basepoint strip v avoids $D_0$ by step 1.1, and hence lies on the old side of C. Its product with c is an actual $J'_t$ strip by step 2.1 and has zero basepoint degree. Steps 5.1--6.1 show that these two constructions are inverse on ALL actual zero-basepoint strips, not just on formal domains or extracted limits. Under the actual product target chart along $(v,c)$ its linearization and boundary spaces split as $$P_{(v,c)}=P_v\oplus D_0.$$ There are no coupling terms: on the whole product component the structure is exactly $J_t\times i$ and its old block is independent of the torus coordinate. The torus summand is the bounded isomorphism [F4]. Thus the actual index is unchanged, kernel and cokernel are those of $P_v$, and regularity is inherited. Translation acts only on v when it is nonconstant, so the rigid orbit bijection and all its finite counts follow. No regular perturbation of the split component is needed. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 The finite differential matrices are identical under $I(x)=x\times c$, by step 7.1 and the old actual count convention. Both count before quotient at index one and then divide by the same nonconstant translation action; no artificial factor comes from the constant torus component. Consequently $d'I=I\,d$, and $P$ is its literal inverse on the full finite generator module. Thus $Pd'=dP$, $PI=\mathrm{Id}$ and $IP=\mathrm{Id}$. Their inverse homotopies are zero. The new square-zero and finite-count properties follow from the identical OLD matrix, whose genuine count realization was just verified. This proves actual stabilization and destabilization maps for the chosen hat complexes. [F1, step 7.1, step 6.2, construct, algebra]

9.1 If $g=0$, the old target is a point with its empty generator. Its stabilization is the same one-intersection torus diagram. Choose its flat structure and a basepoint away from its two circles. There is one generator, and the lift and actual inverse proof of step 6.1 makes every finite-energy strip constant of index zero; its rigid differential is empty. Its sole complementary region gives no nonzero periodic domain with zero basepoint coefficient. Thus both diagrams have the one-dimensional zero-differential complex, and the same I,P give exact inverse chain maps. In all genera the argument retains arbitrary closed Y: it uses only the actual ordinary geometric stabilization and the local zero-basepoint splitting, not an $S^3$ knot-specialized disk theorem. It proves this move operation and does not infer the remaining isotopy/handleslide, positive-basepoint stabilization or grading claims. [F1, F4, A1, step 6.1, step 8.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Give an actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere $Y$, with transverse attaching systems, one-ball compression cuts on both sides, reference orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure and positive area form, and basepoint $z$ off the curves. Broad smooth tangencies of auxiliary compression-disk witnesses are permitted.

There is a CHOICE of surface complex structure, protected region and marked-divisor neighborhoods, common product-integrable generator charts and a smooth nearly symmetric tame path constant on genuine endpoint time collars, for which every nonconstant finite-energy strip with $n_z=0$ has onto actual fixed-end Cauchy--Riemann operator. There are finitely many actual index-one strip orbits with $n_z=0$, across all endpoints and Whitney classes. Their modulo-two matrix on the finite generator space is an actual differential: $\widehat\partial^2=0$. Thus these chosen data define a finite chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ by the stated holomorphic counts.

Within every component of the groupoid of zero-basepoint Whitney classes, its integer relative grading is well defined up to an additive constant, with difference $M(x)-M(y)=\mu(\phi)$ for a class $\phi:x\to y$ with $n_z(\phi)=0$; the counted differential lowers it by one. This does not identify those components with Spin-c structures or assign absolute degrees.

This is a chosen-data existence and well-definedness result on rational homology spheres. It does not replace the broader closed-manifold scope: general $Y$ admissibility, invariance under auxiliary choices and Heegaard moves, absolute grading, Spin-c identifications and any plus/infinity/cobordism package remain separate. It makes no assertion that a possibly empty positive-genus generator set has nonzero homology. For genus zero the target is a point, and its one-generator complex has zero differential.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The actual complete singly pointed splitting and reference complex structure, $H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$, positive area form and basepoint.

[F1] Proper compression disks have same-boundary neat replacements and smooth cut-ball parametrizations after transporting an abstract handlebody to its standard embedded model. These data supply an actual finite oriented surface polygon. A prescribed positive local surface germ extends to a supported disk diffeomorphism with identity boundary collar. ([[lem-proper-compression-disks-admit-neat-witnesses-with-standard-cut-balls]], [[lem-neat-balanced-handlebody-cuts-supply-finite-surface-polygons]], [[lem-smooth-jordan-disk-boundary-maps-extend-to-diffeomorphisms]])

[F2] Every full-curve periodic domain of this complete rational homology sphere diagram is $c\Sigma$, and a zero-basepoint one is zero. Actual zero-basepoint strips therefore have one domain per ordered endpoint pair and uniformly bounded energy on small fixed-geometry families. ([[lem-rational-homology-sphere-heegaard-periodic-domains-are-constant]], [[lem-rational-homology-sphere-zero-marked-strips-have-uniform-energy-bounds]])

[F3] Continuous classes admit actual smooth fixed-end models, with homotopy-invariant additive actual index and additive point-divisor degrees. Differences of same-end smooth domains are full-curve periodic; equal domains give equal actual indices, with the supplied finite surface polygon. ([[lem-continuous-whitney-classes-admit-relative-smooth-fixed-end-models]], [[lem-smooth-relative-whitney-homotopies-preserve-strip-fredholm-index]], [[lem-symmetric-product-divisor-intersections-and-point-movement]], [[lem-equal-whitney-domains-have-equal-boundary-windings-and-fredholm-index]])

[F4] The domain-energy estimate is $E(u)\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta$, with one common $C$ on a sufficiently small fixed protected coefficient family. Auxiliary flat-endpoint-jet all-strip regular paths have actual constant-collar approximants regular on EVERY nonconstant zero-marked strip below any specified finite energy bound. The compact cut systems must each have a chosen zero mark in every cut component; here the single basepoint does so. ([[lem-nearly-symmetric-heegaard-strip-domain-energy-bound]], [[thm-countable-choice-flat-endpoint-jet-universal-strip-regularity]], [[lem-zero-marked-bounded-energy-strip-regularity-survives-collar-approximation]])

[F5] For a path regular on all zero-marked strips below $E_*$, the actual index-one orbits below that energy are finite. For each fixed zero-marked index-two class $\phi$, if $E_*>B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta$, the actual compactified one-manifold has finitely many broken rigid ends and gives their modulo-two cancellation. These results apply to general compact Heegaard data, without a torsion Spin-c or knot premise. ([[thm-finite-zero-marked-actual-index-one-strip-counts-under-an-energy-bound]], [[thm-fixed-zero-marked-whitney-class-index-two-compactification-and-mod-two-cancellation]])

## Proof

1.1 If the genus is zero, the target is a point and the stated one-generator zero differential and grading follow directly; assume henceforth positive genus. Prepare the geometric data without a category narrowing. View either actual handlebody as an abstract regular neighborhood of its finite graph, transport it to the standard ball-with-handles model embedded in $S^3$, apply [F1]'s broad same-boundary compression preparation there and transport back. The surface, attaching circles and diagram in $Y$ are unchanged. The resulting one-ball cut supplies the actual finite polygon needed by [F3]. To choose genuine integrable crossing charts, at each of finitely many crossings take a positive smooth chart $\Psi$ straightening the two arcs and an old holomorphic chart $c$. The positive local germ $c^{-1}\Psi$ fixes that crossing. Extend it by [F1] to a diffeomorphism supported in a small crossing disk, identity near its boundary. Choose these disks disjoint and off all chosen region points and $z$. Their finite composite $F$ gives the actual integrable structure $j=F^*j_{\mathrm{ref}}$; the charts $cF=\Psi$ are holomorphic, with unchanged holomorphic transition maps. Their products give common $\mathbb R^h/i\mathbb R^h$ generator charts in $\operatorname{Sym}^h\Sigma$. Choose protected diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods separated from the two compact tori and smaller generator charts, and use the constant standard background path. No interpolation of surface complex structures has been presumed integrable. [F1, F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Obtain an energy bound BEFORE choosing regular counts or rigid pairs. For each ordered generator pair admitting a continuous Whitney class of basepoint degree zero, its smooth models in [F3] have a UNIQUE region domain $D_{xy}$: the difference of two such models is full-curve periodic with basepoint coefficient zero, hence vanishes by [F2]. This argument uses arbitrary smooth models, not just holomorphic representatives. Choose one actual class witness for each nonempty pair; the generator set and the choices are finite. Let $C$ be uniform on the small protected family in [F4], and put $$B=\max\left(\{C\sum_R|n_R(D_{xy})|\int_R\eta\}_{x,y}\cup\{0\}\right),\qquad E_*=B+1.$$ Every actual zero-basepoint strip has energy at most $B$ by [F4], independent of its index. Moreover EVERY zero-basepoint class $\phi$ has $B_\phi\le B$, since its domain is that same $D_{xy}$. This includes classes later formed by concatenating rigid pairs. Thus the bound does not depend on which pairs turn out to be holomorphic for the chosen path. If there are no such pairs use $B=0$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Use the zero-mark set consisting ONLY of $z$; the additional protected region divisors are not required to have zero degree. Choose in this protected family an auxiliary all-strip regular flat-jet path from [F4]. Its genuine constant-collar approximants have the same surface, boundary structures, generator charts and common energy constant. The bounded-energy zero-marked openness theorem in [F4] makes every sufficiently late approximant regular on every nonconstant zero-basepoint strip of energy at most $E_*$. Fix one. Step 2.1 bounds ALL of its actual zero-basepoint strips by $B<E_*$, so it is regular for all of them, including every possible limiting level; no negative-index nonregular level is left uncontrolled. This also implies each nonconstant such strip has positive actual index, since its nonzero longitudinal derivative is a square-integrable kernel section by its exact end decay and onto-ness. Applying the actual finite-count assertion in [F5] now gives finitely many index-one orbits across every generator pair and represented class. Their modulo-two finite sums define a matrix on the finite vector space. [F4, F5, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix initial and final generators. A term in the coefficient of their differential square is an ordered pair of these finitely many rigid orbits. Its concatenated continuous class $\phi$ has zero basepoint degree and actual index two by [F3]. There are only finitely many such ordered pairs and hence finitely many such concatenated classes; distinct classes with identical domains are not identified. For EACH of these actual classes step 2.1 gives $B_\phi\le B<E_*$. The chosen path is regular on its entire required zero-basepoint energy range by step 3.1, so [F5]'s fixed-class compactification and parity theorem apply. Its boundary pairs are exactly all the rigid orbit pairs whose concatenated class is this $\phi$. Their number is even. Summing this identity over the finite list of actual concatenated classes exhausts the coefficient of the differential square and makes it zero in $\mathbb F_2$. No summation over merely formal domains, no finiteness assumption for arbitrary class sets, and no positive-mark boundary-degeneration theorem were used. [F3, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 For the relative grading, use the groupoid whose arrows are zero-basepoint continuous classes with concatenation. Reversal negates degree and index by [F3]. Any loop arrow at a generator has periodic domain with zero basepoint degree, so its domain is zero by [F2]. Comparing with the actual constant model by [F3] gives index zero. Two arrows with the same endpoints therefore have the same index by composing with a reversal; alternatively their equal domains give the same conclusion directly. On a nonempty groupoid component fix one generator, assign it degree zero and assign every other generator minus the index of any arrow from that one. Index additivity and the preceding independence prove the stated differences, with uniqueness up to a componentwise additive constant. Only finitely many generator components occur, and no Spin-c interpretation or absolute shift is inferred. Each counted arrow has index one, so its differential term lowers this degree by one. In genus zero the symmetric product is a point and the sole generator has no index-one strips, giving the stated one-generator zero differential directly. This proves the chosen-data finite complex only; broader closed-manifold existence, invariance and graded packages remain separate. [F2, F3, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎
